## 2. Tables — Full Catalogue

### 2.1 `app_settings` — Runtime Configuration

| Key | Default | Description |
|-----|---------|-------------|
| `geo_max_accuracy_m` | 100 | Reject GPS less accurate than this (m) |
| `geo_default_radius_m` | 150 | Geofence radius when event doesn't set one (m) |
| `geo_max_fix_age_sec` | 60 | Reject GPS fixes older than this (s) |
| `geo_checkin_window_before_min` | 30 | Minutes before `start_at` geo window opens |
| `otp_max_requests_per_hour` | 5 | OTP rate limit per phone/hour |
| `otp_max_attempts` | 5 | Wrong OTP attempts before lockout |
| `otp_ttl_minutes` | 5 | OTP lifetime |

Fetched via `setting_int(key TEXT)` — a stable SQL function.

---

### 2.2 `charity_fields` — Lookup Table

Pre-seeded activity categories used to tag both users (interests) and events.

**13 built-in codes:** `teaching`, `food_distribution`, `elderly_care`, `child_care`, `animal_welfare`, `environment`, `disaster_support`, `blood_donation`, `fundraising`, `logistics`, `cleaning`, `cooking`, `other`.

---

### 2.3 `users` — Accounts

The central entity. Phone is **never stored in plaintext** — only `phone_hash` (HMAC) for lookups and `phone_enc` (encrypted) for display.

| Field | Notes |
|-------|-------|
| `account_status` | `active` / `blocked` / `closed` |
| `is_active` | Derived from `account_status = 'active'` (kept in sync by trigger) |
| `is_admin / is_staff / is_superuser` | Staff/superuser imply admin; only admins can set these |
| `verification_status` | `none` / `pending` / `verified` / `rejected` — **derived by trigger** from `user_verification_images` |
| `blood_type` | `A+`, `A-`, `B+`, `B-`, `AB+`, `AB-`, `O+`, `O-`, `unknown` |
| `skills` | `TEXT[]` GIN-indexed, normalized (lowercase, ≤30 tags, ≤50 chars each) |

> [!IMPORTANT]
> `phone_hash` is immutable (enforced by trigger). `is_active` is never written directly — it syncs with `account_status`.

---

### 2.4 `user_charity_interests`

Junction table linking users to `charity_fields`. One row per (user, field). Used for event matching / volunteer dashboard filtering.

---

### 2.5 `volunteer_availability_rules`

Recurring **weekly windows** (weekday 1–7, time range). Unique on `(user_id, weekday, start_time)`.

### 2.6 `volunteer_availability_exceptions`

**Date-specific overrides** (blackouts or narrow windows). One per `(user_id, date)`.

> Both queried by `is_user_available(user, start, end)` — exception overrides rule; no rules = always available.

---

### 2.7 `coordinator_profiles`

One row per user who is or was a coordinator.

| Status | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `pending` | Awaiting admin approval |
| `approved` | Active coordinator, can own/run events |
| `suspended` | Temporarily disabled |
| `revoked` | Permanently removed |

**State machine:** `pending → approved/revoked`, `approved → suspended/revoked`, `suspended → approved/revoked`

> [!CAUTION]
> Approval requires the approver to be an active admin AND the user to have `verification_status = 'verified'`. Self-approval is blocked by `CHECK`.

---

### 2.8 `user_verification_images`

Stores **server-side paths** to JPEG identity documents (never the bytes).

| Field | Values |
|-------|--------|
| `image_type` | `mock_selfie`, `id_license`, `driver_license` |
| `status` | `pending` → `approved` / `rejected` |
| `comparison_status` | `pending`, `match`, `no_match`, `needs_review` |
| `is_current` | Unique index ensures one current image per type per user |

Trigger `trg_50_vimg_after` calls `recompute_user_verification()` on every change, which updates `users.verification_status`.

**Verified = approved `mock_selfie` + approved `id_license` or `driver_license`.**

---

### 2.9 `auth_otp`

Short-lived OTP tokens. Only cryptographic **hashes** are stored (`phone_hash` and `code_hash`). The database enforces strict rate limits (`trg_01_otp_rate_limit`: max 5 requests/hr per `phone_hash`) and attempt limits (max 3-5 verification attempts before invalidation).

| Field | Type | Constraints & Notes |
|-------|------|-------------------|
| `id` | `BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY` | Primary key |
| `phone_hash` | `TEXT NOT NULL` | HMAC-SHA256 of normalized E.164 phone |
| `code_hash` | `TEXT NOT NULL` | HMAC-SHA256 of raw OTP code (never plaintext) |
| `purpose` | `TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'login'` | Check: `'login'` or `'qr_registration'` |
| `attempt_count` | `INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` | Check: between `0` and `100` |
| `expires_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL` | Check: `expires_at > created_at` (default `now() + 5m`) |
| `consumed_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | NULL = unconsumed; Check: `consumed_at >= created_at` |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()` | Insertion timestamp |

**Indexes:**
- `idx_auth_otp_phone_created`: `(phone_hash, created_at DESC)`
- `idx_auth_otp_open`: `(phone_hash, purpose) WHERE consumed_at IS NULL`
- `idx_auth_otp_expires`: `(expires_at)`

> [!NOTE]
> **Tokenization Architecture Compatibility:** Under the new Tokenization Login architecture (`docs/tokenization_login_architecture.md`), this table and its triggers require **zero schema changes**. The Django BFF detokenizes the incoming Client Identity Token (CIT) into `phone_hash`, issues an ephemeral `auth_session_token` in application cache, and invokes `request_otp()` and `verify_otp()` against this authoritative table.

---

### 2.10 `events`

The core operational table.

| Field | Values / Notes |
|-------|---------------|
| `status` | `draft → published → active → completed / cancelled` |
| `acceptance_mode` | `auto` (auto-accept up to capacity) / `manual` (coordinator decides) |
| `purpose_type` | `charity_event` / `help_wanted_event` |
| `leader_strategy` | `none` / `first_experienced` / `manual` |
| `geo_checkin_enabled` | Requires `latitude`/`longitude` |
| `geo_radius_m` | 20–5000 m; NULL = `app_settings.geo_default_radius_m` |
| `map_provider` | `openstreetmap` / `google` |
| `compensation_kind` | `unpaid` / `arranged_outside_system` |
| `onboarding_version` | Auto-incremented by trigger whenever `onboarding_text` changes |
| `owner_id` | Immutable after creation |
| `current_coordinator_id` | Changeable via `change_event_coordinator()` |

**Lifecycle timestamps** are enforced by `CHECK` — e.g. `published` status requires `published_at IS NOT NULL AND activated_at IS NULL`.

> [!WARNING]
> Completed and cancelled events are **frozen** — only soft-delete columns (`deleted_at`, `deleted_by_id`) may change.

---

### 2.11 `event_coordinator_history`

Append-only log of every coordinator change. First row is inserted automatically on event creation.

---

### 2.12 `event_charity_fields`

Many-to-many: event ↔ charity_fields. Cascade-deletes with event.

---

### 2.13 `event_posts` — Roles Within an Event

Each event has one or more posts representing specific jobs.

| Field | Notes |
|-------|-------|
| `required_headcount` | 1–100,000 |
| `physical_level` | `none` / `light` / `medium` / `heavy` |
| `required_skills` | `TEXT[]` matched against `users.skills` |
| `status` | `open` / `full` (auto-maintained by trigger) / `closed` (set by coordinator) |
| `priority` | Lower = filled first during auto-assignment |

---

### 2.14 `qr_tokens`

Only the **hash** of the token is stored (never the raw secret).

| `purpose` | Use |
|-----------|-----|
| `walkin_registration` | Scan to submit a walk-in application |
| `checkin` | Scan to check in to a shift |
| `join_event` | Generic event join |

Revocable. `used_count` can only increase. Event completion/cancellation auto-revokes all open tokens.

---

### 2.15 `event_applications`

| `status` | Transition |
|----------|-----------|
| `pending` | Initial; awaits coordinator or auto-accept |
| `accepted` | Triggers assignment creation |
| `waitlisted` | Capacity full; promoted if space opens |
| `rejected` | By coordinator |
| `withdrawn` | By volunteer |
| `expired` | Auto-set when event ends |

| `source` | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| `browse` | Normal app apply |
| `qr_walkin` | Walk-in QR scan; stays `pending` even in auto mode |
| `invite` | Coordinator-initiated |

**One active application per user per event** (unique partial index on `pending/accepted/waitlisted`).

---

### 2.16 `assignments`

Created automatically when an application is accepted (if `auto_assign_enabled`) or manually by a coordinator.

| `status` | Transition |
|----------|-----------|
| `assigned` | Default |
| `confirmed` | Volunteer confirms their own shift |
| `completed` | Set when event completes |
| `cancelled` | Volunteer or coordinator |

**No scheduling overlap:** `EXCLUDE USING gist (user_id WITH =, tstzrange(...) WITH &&)` — a volunteer cannot hold two overlapping active assignments.

**Group logic:** When `events.group_size` is set, volunteers are auto-grouped into `G1`, `G2`, etc. The first experienced volunteer in a group becomes leader (if `leader_strategy = 'first_experienced'`).

---

### 2.17 `attendance`

One row per assignment. Created automatically when an assignment is inserted.

| `status` | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| `expected` | Assignment exists, not yet present |
| `checked_in` | Present (geo/QR/manual) |
| `absent` | Marked absent by coordinator |
| `completed` | Cascaded from event completion |
| `cancelled` | Cascaded from assignment cancellation |

| `method` | Who sets it |
|----------|------------|
| `qr_scan` | Volunteer scans coordinator's QR |
| `geo` | Volunteer's device GPS |
| `coordinator_manual` | Coordinator marks manually |
| `system` | Automated |

**Geo check-ins** (`method = 'geo'`) require coordinator confirmation when `require_checkin_confirmation = TRUE`. On rejection, the status reverts to `expected` and all geo evidence is cleared (kept in `attendance_geo_attempts`).

> [!NOTE]
> Walk-in volunteers (`walk_in_flag = TRUE`) cannot use geo check-in — QR or manual only.

---

### 2.18 `attendance_geo_attempts`

**Anti-fraud evidence log** — every geo check-in attempt (accepted or rejected) is recorded here. Rows are **append-only** (delete and mutation blocked by trigger). Coordinates are purged after 90 days by `purge_geo_evidence()`.

Result codes: `accepted`, `already_checked_in`, `invalid_fix`, `low_accuracy`, `stale_fix`, `mock_location`, `outside_geofence`, `window_closed`, `event_not_active`, `geo_disabled`, `not_assigned`, `not_eligible`, `onboarding_required`.

---

### 2.19 `onboarding_acknowledgments`

Append-only. A volunteer must acknowledge the **current version** of the onboarding text before they can check in. Version auto-increments when `events.onboarding_text` changes.

---

### 2.20 `feedback`

Post-event ratings (1–5). Three directions:

| Direction | Who rates whom |
|-----------|---------------|
| `coordinator_to_volunteer` | Owner/coordinator rates an assigned volunteer |
| `volunteer_to_event` | Attended volunteer rates the event (no `target_user_id`) |
| `volunteer_to_coordinator` | Attended volunteer rates the owner/coordinator |

One feedback per (rater, event, direction, target). Only submittable after event is `completed`. **Immutable after submission** — only admins can hide via moderation.

---

### 2.21 `moderation_actions`

**Insert-only action log** — inserting a row *applies* the action via trigger.

| `action_type` | Effect |
|---------------|--------|
| `user_warning` | No status change; logged only |
| `user_block` | Sets `account_status = 'blocked'` |
| `user_unblock` | Restores `account_status = 'active'` |
| `account_close` | Sets `account_status = 'closed'` |
| `account_reinstate` | Reopens closed account |
| `event_delete` | Soft-deletes event (`deleted_at`) |
| `event_restore` | Clears soft-delete |
| `event_cancel` | Cancels event (cascades assignments/applications) |
| `feedback_hide` | Sets `feedback.status = 'hidden'` |

Admin accounts cannot be blocked/closed via this table (only warned).

---

### 2.22 `audit_logs`

Append-only audit trail written by `trg_audit_row()` triggers on all key tables. Secrets (`phone_enc`, `password`, `token_hash`, `code_hash`) and noise columns (`updated_at`, `last_login`) are stripped. Coordinates are excluded from attendance audit. Only changed columns are stored for UPDATEs.

---

## 3. Business Rules & Logic

### 3.1 State Machines

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    direction LR
    state "Event" as E {
        [*] --> draft
        draft --> published : has open post + future start
        draft --> cancelled
        published --> active
        published --> cancelled
        active --> completed
        active --> cancelled
    }
    state "Application" as A {
        [*] --> pending
        pending --> accepted
        pending --> waitlisted
        pending --> rejected
        pending --> withdrawn
        pending --> expired
        waitlisted --> accepted
        waitlisted --> rejected
        waitlisted --> withdrawn
        waitlisted --> expired
        accepted --> withdrawn
        accepted --> expired
    }
    state "Assignment" as AS {
        [*] --> assigned
        assigned --> confirmed
        assigned --> cancelled
        assigned --> completed
        confirmed --> cancelled
        confirmed --> completed
    }
    state "Attendance" as AT {
        [*] --> expected
        expected --> checked_in
        expected --> absent
        expected --> cancelled
        checked_in --> completed
        checked_in --> expected : geo rejected
        absent --> checked_in
        cancelled --> expected
    }
    state "Coordinator" as C {
        [*] --> pending
        pending --> approved
        pending --> revoked
        approved --> suspended
        approved --> revoked
        suspended --> approved
        suspended --> revoked
    }
```

### 3.2 Key Trigger Chains

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["INSERT user_verification_images"]
    B["trg_01_vimg_guard\nForces status=pending\nRetires old is_current"]
    C["trg_50_vimg_after\nrecompute_user_verification()"]
    D["UPDATE users.verification_status"]

    A --> B --> C --> D

    E["INSERT event_applications\n(acceptance_mode=auto)"]
    F["trg_01_applications_before_insert\nAuto-accepts if capacity available"]
    G["trg_50_applications_after\ncreate_assignment_from_application()"]
    H["trg_50_assignments_after_insert\nINSERT attendance row (expected)"]

    E --> F --> G --> H

    I["UPDATE events SET status='cancelled'"]
    J["trg_50_events_after_update\nCancel active assignments\nExpire pending applications\nRevoke QR tokens"]

    I --> J

    K["INSERT moderation_actions\n(action_type='user_block')"]
    L["trg_01_moderation_before_insert\nVerify actor is admin"]
    M["trg_50_moderation_after_insert\nUPDATE users.account_status='blocked'"]

    K --> L --> M
```

### 3.3 Auto-Assignment Algorithm

1. **Lock** the event row (serializes capacity decisions)
2. **Skip** if user already has a conflicting schedule (`user_has_schedule_conflict`)
3. **Find** the first open post matching: skills overlap, physical capability, new-volunteer policy, and remaining headcount — ordered by `priority ASC`
4. **Determine group:** find the lowest `Gn` with space (< `group_size`)
5. **Assign leader** if `has_leader_experience AND leader_strategy = 'first_experienced'` and no leader yet in that group

### 3.4 Geo Check-In Pipeline

```
Volunteer sends (lat, lon, accuracy, captured_at, is_mocked)
         ↓
1. Event must be `active` and `geo_checkin_enabled`
2. Volunteer must have an `assigned` or `confirmed` assignment (not walk-in)
3. Must be within geo window: (start_at - before_min) ≤ now ≤ end_at
4. Onboarding must be acknowledged (current version)
5. Fix must not be mocked, stale (> 60s), or low-accuracy (> 100m)
6. Distance = Haversine formula → must be ≤ geo_radius_m
         ↓
Every attempt (pass or fail) → attendance_geo_attempts
         ↓
On success: attendance.status = 'checked_in', geo fields set
  If require_checkin_confirmation: confirmation_status = 'pending'
  Coordinator must confirm_attendance() or reject_attendance()
  On reject: attendance reverts to 'expected', evidence cleared
```

### 3.5 OTP Flow

```
request_otp(phone_hash, code_hash, purpose)
  → rate-limit trigger: max 5/hr per phone
  → INSERT auth_otp (expires in otp_ttl_minutes = 5m)

verify_otp(phone_hash, code_hash, purpose)
  → SELECT latest unconsumed OTP FOR UPDATE
  → Check: not expired, attempt_count < 5
  → Match: UPDATE consumed_at → return 'ok'
  → Mismatch: increment attempt_count → return 'invalid_code'
```

### 3.6 Permission Model (Row-Level via Session Variable)

```sql
-- App layer sets before each request:
SET app.user_id = '<user_id>';
SET app.ip = '<client_ip>';
```

| Capability | Who |
|-----------|-----|
| Create events | Approved coordinator only |
| Publish/activate events | Event owner or current coordinator |
| Decide applications | Event manager (owner, coordinator, or admin) |
| Confirm/reject check-ins | Event manager |
| Change coordinator | Owner, current coordinator, or admin |
| Review verification images | Admin only |
| Moderate users/events | Admin only |
| Self-confirm assignment | Volunteer only |
| Self-acknowledge onboarding | Volunteer only |
| Self-check-in (QR/geo) | Volunteer only |

### 3.7 Privacy & Immutability Rules

| Table / Column | Rule |
|----------------|------|
| `users.phone_hash` | Immutable after creation |
| `events.owner_id` | Immutable after creation |
| `audit_logs` | Append-only (UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE blocked) |
| `moderation_actions` | Append-only |
| `event_coordinator_history` | Append-only |
| `onboarding_acknowledgments` | Append-only |
| `attendance_geo_attempts` | Append-only; coordinates nullable (purge after 90 days) |
| Audit log | Never contains `phone_enc`, `password`, `token_hash`, `code_hash`, or GPS coordinates |
| `user_verification_images` | Image path/hash immutable; can only review once (pending → decided) |
| `feedback` | Immutable after submission; only admins can hide via moderation |

## 7. Self-Test Coverage (`self_test.sql`)

The self-test runs in a single transaction and **rolls back** at the end (non-destructive). It verifies:

| Area | Tests |
|------|-------|
| Availability rules | Time order, weekday range, exception time pair, duplicate rejection |
| `is_user_available()` | No-rules=TRUE, within-window=TRUE, exception-blocks=FALSE |
| Privilege protection | Staff flag requires admin; non-admin cannot elevate themselves |
| Event creation | Draft start, coordinator defaulting, map provider validation |
| Auto-accept + assignment | Application auto-accepted in `auto` mode, group leader assigned |
| State machine | Invalid event status transitions rejected |
| Lifecycle timestamps | `published_at`, `activated_at`, `completed_at` set correctly |
| Walk-in QR flow | Application stays pending even in auto mode, `walk_in_flag=TRUE` |
| Onboarding gate | Geo check-in blocked until onboarding acknowledged |
| Geo check-in | Outside geofence, low accuracy, mock location, stale fix, success path |
| Geo idempotency | Repeat scan does not spend another attempt |
| Geo confirmation | Volunteer cannot confirm own check-in |
| Rejection + retry | Evidence cleared on rejection; volunteer can try again |
| QR check-in | Used-count limits enforced |
| Assignment cancellation | Cascades attendance to `cancelled` |
| Coordinator handover | Non-manager cannot hand over; owner unchanged |
| Event completion | Cascades attendance + assignments; event is frozen after |
| Feedback rules | Only participants can leave feedback; excluded volunteers rejected |
| Moderation | Block applies; blocked user cannot unblock themselves |
| Audit trail | >20 rows generated; no GPS in audit log; append-only enforced |

# Local Database Alteration Guide: v0.12.0 Tokenized OTP Challenge Handshake

**Document ID:** `DOC-LOCAL-DB-ALTER-v0.12.0`  
**Target Engine:** PostgreSQL 14+ (Database-First Architecture)  
**Database Name:** `volunteer_coordination_db` (default)  
**Additive Upgrade Script:** `postgres_sql/v0_12_0_auth_otp_challenge_upgrade.sql`  
**Master Database Script:** `postgres_sql/updated_volunteer_coordination_system_Database.sql`  
**Automated Python Helper:** `scripts/alter_local_db.py`  

---

## 1. Overview: What Changed & Why

In Release **v0.12.0**, the authentication subsystem was upgraded from the legacy OTP verification flow to a secure, session-bound **Tokenized OTP Challenge Handshake**. 

### The Problem with the Legacy Flow
- The mobile client had to send the raw user `phone` number again during the verify step (`POST /api/v1/auth/verify-otp/`).
- The database had to query for the latest unconsumed OTP matching the phone hash, which was vulnerable to concurrent race conditions and OTP reuse.

### The v0.12.0 Handshake Architecture
- **Step 1 (Request OTP):** `POST /api/v1/auth/tokenized/request-otp/` takes the phone number, generates a 6-digit OTP, creates an `auth_otp` record, and issues a 256-bit cryptographic `auth_session_token`.
- **Step 2 (Verify OTP):** `POST /api/v1/auth/tokenized/verify-otp/` requires **ONLY** `auth_session_token` and the 6-digit `code`. The phone number is **never transmitted** during verification.
- **Database Enforcement:** PostgreSQL directly enforces dual-clock TTL expiry (challenge TTL capped at 180s), deterministic row locking (`FOR UPDATE`), single-use consumption, and code attempt limits.

### Safety Guarantee
This migration is **100% additive and safe for existing data**:
- **No data loss:** Existing `users`, `events`, `attendance`, `profiles`, and active `auth_otp` rows remain completely intact.
- **Dual compatibility:** Legacy OTP endpoints remain operational alongside the new tokenized routes during the migration period.

---

## 2. Summary of Database Schema Changes

The migration introduces the following new objects to your PostgreSQL database:

| Object Type | Name | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Table** | `auth_otp_challenge` | Stores tokenized challenge sessions tied to `auth_otp(id)` via `ON DELETE CASCADE`. Stores `HMAC-SHA256` token hash (never raw token). |
| **Index** | `idx_auth_otp_challenge_otp_id` | B-tree index on foreign key `otp_id` for fast navigation and cascading deletions. |
| **Index** | `idx_auth_otp_challenge_expires` | Partial B-tree index on `(expires_at) WHERE consumed_at IS NULL` for rapid lookup of active challenges. |
| **Index** | `idx_auth_otp_challenge_nonce` | Unique partial index on `identity_nonce_hash` for replay attack prevention. |
| **Trigger Function** | `trg_auth_otp_challenge_before()` | Validates invariants: `challenge.expires_at <= otp.expires_at` and `challenge.purpose == otp.purpose`. |
| **Trigger** | `trg_01_auth_otp_challenge_guard` | `BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE` trigger bound to `auth_otp_challenge`. |
| **Stored Function** | `create_otp_challenge(...)` | Atomic function to issue challenge, clamp TTL to $\le 180$s and parent OTP expiry, and return new challenge ID. |
| **Stored Function** | `verify_otp_challenge(...)` | Atomic function using deterministic row locking (`auth_otp_challenge` then `auth_otp` `FOR UPDATE`), checking single-use consumption, dual clocks, attempt limits, and hash verification. |
| **Retention Function** | `purge_expired_otp_challenges(...)` | Cleans up consumed or expired challenges older than retention period (default 1 day). Leaves active challenges untouched. |
| **Retention Function** | `purge_expired_otps()` | Updated to invoke `purge_expired_otp_challenges(INTERVAL '1 day')` before purging parent OTP records. |

## 4. Complete SQL Migration Script (Copy-Pasteable)

If you prefer to copy and paste the raw SQL directly into any SQL editor, use the complete block below:

```sql
-- =============================================================================
-- Migration: v0.12.0 Additive Upgrade — OTP Challenge Table & Stored Functions
-- File: postgres_sql/v0_12_0_auth_otp_challenge_upgrade.sql
-- Target Database: PostgreSQL 14+ (Volunteer Coordination System)
-- =============================================================================

BEGIN;

-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. Table: auth_otp_challenge
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS auth_otp_challenge (
    id                   BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    otp_id               BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES auth_otp (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    challenge_token_hash TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    purpose              TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'login',
    created_at           TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    expires_at           TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    consumed_at          TIMESTAMPTZ,
    request_id           TEXT,
    identity_nonce_hash  TEXT,

    CONSTRAINT ck_auth_otp_challenge_purpose
        CHECK (purpose IN ('login', 'qr_registration')),
    CONSTRAINT ck_auth_otp_challenge_token_hash_len
        CHECK (length(challenge_token_hash) = 64),
    CONSTRAINT ck_auth_otp_challenge_expiry
        CHECK (expires_at > created_at),
    CONSTRAINT ck_auth_otp_challenge_consumed
        CHECK (consumed_at IS NULL OR consumed_at >= created_at)
);

-- Indexes for challenge lookups and expiry scans
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_auth_otp_challenge_otp_id
    ON auth_otp_challenge (otp_id);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_auth_otp_challenge_expires
    ON auth_otp_challenge (expires_at)
    WHERE consumed_at IS NULL;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_auth_otp_challenge_nonce
    ON auth_otp_challenge (identity_nonce_hash)
    WHERE identity_nonce_hash IS NOT NULL;

-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. Trigger Function: Enforce Challenge Expiry <= Parent auth_otp Expiry
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION trg_auth_otp_challenge_before()
RETURNS TRIGGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
    v_otp auth_otp%ROWTYPE;
BEGIN
    SELECT * INTO v_otp FROM auth_otp WHERE id = NEW.otp_id;
    IF NOT FOUND THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'invalid_otp_reference: referenced auth_otp row (%) does not exist', NEW.otp_id;
    END IF;

    -- Invariant: Challenge expiry cannot exceed parent OTP expiry
    IF NEW.expires_at > v_otp.expires_at THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'challenge_expiry_exceeds_otp: challenge expires_at (%) cannot exceed auth_otp expires_at (%)',
            NEW.expires_at, v_otp.expires_at;
    END IF;

    -- Invariant: Challenge purpose must match parent OTP purpose
    IF NEW.purpose <> v_otp.purpose THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'purpose_mismatch: challenge purpose (%) must match auth_otp purpose (%)',
            NEW.purpose, v_otp.purpose;
    END IF;

    RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_01_auth_otp_challenge_guard ON auth_otp_challenge;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_01_auth_otp_challenge_guard
    BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON auth_otp_challenge
    FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION trg_auth_otp_challenge_before();

-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. Stored Function: create_otp_challenge
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION create_otp_challenge(
    p_otp_id               BIGINT,
    p_challenge_token_hash TEXT,
    p_ttl_seconds          INTEGER DEFAULT 180,
    p_purpose              TEXT DEFAULT 'login',
    p_request_id           TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
    p_identity_nonce_hash  TEXT DEFAULT NULL
)
RETURNS BIGINT
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
    v_otp          auth_otp%ROWTYPE;
    v_challenge_id BIGINT;
    v_expires_at   TIMESTAMPTZ;
BEGIN
    SELECT * INTO v_otp FROM auth_otp WHERE id = p_otp_id;
    IF NOT FOUND THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'invalid_otp_reference: referenced auth_otp row (%) does not exist', p_otp_id;
    END IF;

    -- Capped at max 180s challenge TTL and parent OTP expiry: min(issued_at + 180s, otp.expires_at)
    v_expires_at := LEAST(now() + make_interval(secs => LEAST(p_ttl_seconds, 180)), v_otp.expires_at);

    INSERT INTO auth_otp_challenge (
        otp_id,
        challenge_token_hash,
        purpose,
        expires_at,
        request_id,
        identity_nonce_hash
    )
    VALUES (
        p_otp_id,
        p_challenge_token_hash,
        p_purpose,
        v_expires_at,
        p_request_id,
        p_identity_nonce_hash
    )
    RETURNING id INTO v_challenge_id;

    RETURN v_challenge_id;
END;
$$;

-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 4. Stored Function: verify_otp_challenge (Atomic, Deterministic Locking)
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION verify_otp_challenge(
    p_challenge_token_hash TEXT,
    p_code_hash            TEXT,
    p_purpose              TEXT DEFAULT 'login'
)
RETURNS TABLE (
    status     TEXT,
    phone_hash TEXT,
    otp_id     BIGINT
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
    v_chal auth_otp_challenge%ROWTYPE;
    v_otp  auth_otp%ROWTYPE;
BEGIN
    -- Step 1: Deterministic locking order — lock challenge row first
    SELECT * INTO v_chal
      FROM auth_otp_challenge
     WHERE challenge_token_hash = p_challenge_token_hash
       FOR UPDATE;

    IF NOT FOUND THEN
        RETURN QUERY SELECT 'invalid_challenge'::TEXT, NULL::TEXT, NULL::BIGINT;
        RETURN;
    END IF;

    -- Step 2: Purpose validation
    IF v_chal.purpose <> p_purpose THEN
        RETURN QUERY SELECT 'invalid_challenge'::TEXT, NULL::TEXT, NULL::BIGINT;
        RETURN;
    END IF;

    -- Step 3: Lock linked parent auth_otp row
    SELECT * INTO v_otp
      FROM auth_otp
     WHERE id = v_chal.otp_id
       FOR UPDATE;

    IF NOT FOUND THEN
        RETURN QUERY SELECT 'invalid_challenge'::TEXT, NULL::TEXT, NULL::BIGINT;
        RETURN;
    END IF;

    -- Step 4: Check consumption status (single-use constraint)
    IF v_chal.consumed_at IS NOT NULL OR v_otp.consumed_at IS NOT NULL THEN
        RETURN QUERY SELECT 'challenge_consumed'::TEXT, NULL::TEXT, v_chal.otp_id;
        RETURN;
    END IF;

    -- Step 5: Enforce dual expiry clocks
    IF v_chal.expires_at <= now() OR v_otp.expires_at <= now() THEN
        RETURN QUERY SELECT 'challenge_expired'::TEXT, NULL::TEXT, v_chal.otp_id;
        RETURN;
    END IF;

    -- Step 6: Enforce attempt limit
    IF v_otp.attempt_count >= setting_int('otp_max_attempts') THEN
        RETURN QUERY SELECT 'too_many_attempts'::TEXT, NULL::TEXT, v_chal.otp_id;
        RETURN;
    END IF;

    -- Step 7: Compare code hash
    IF v_otp.code_hash = p_code_hash THEN
        UPDATE auth_otp_challenge SET consumed_at = now() WHERE id = v_chal.id;
        UPDATE auth_otp SET consumed_at = now() WHERE id = v_otp.id;
        RETURN QUERY SELECT 'ok'::TEXT, v_otp.phone_hash, v_otp.id;
        RETURN;
    END IF;

    -- Wrong code: increment attempt counter on the exact bound auth_otp row
    UPDATE auth_otp SET attempt_count = attempt_count + 1 WHERE id = v_otp.id;
    RETURN QUERY SELECT 'invalid_code'::TEXT, NULL::TEXT, v_otp.id;
    RETURN;
END;
$$;

-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 5. Stored Functions: Retention & Cleanup
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION purge_expired_otp_challenges(p_retention INTERVAL DEFAULT INTERVAL '1 day')
RETURNS INTEGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
    v_n INTEGER;
BEGIN
    -- Delete consumed or expired challenges older than retention threshold.
    -- Active challenges (unconsumed where expires_at >= now()) are never deleted.
    DELETE FROM auth_otp_challenge
     WHERE (consumed_at IS NOT NULL AND consumed_at < now() - p_retention)
        OR (expires_at < now() - p_retention);
    GET DIAGNOSTICS v_n = ROW_COUNT;
    RETURN v_n;
END;
$$;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION purge_expired_otps()
RETURNS INTEGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
    v_n INTEGER;
BEGIN
    PERFORM purge_expired_otp_challenges(INTERVAL '1 day');
    DELETE FROM auth_otp
     WHERE expires_at < now() - INTERVAL '1 day'
        OR created_at < now() - INTERVAL '1 day';
    GET DIAGNOSTICS v_n = ROW_COUNT;
    RETURN v_n;
END;
$$;

COMMIT;
```

### 4. Interactive End-to-End Handshake Sanity Test

You can execute this self-cleaning PL/pgSQL block in your SQL editor to test the complete challenge handshake in PostgreSQL:

```sql
DO $$
DECLARE
    v_otp_id   BIGINT;
    v_chal_id  BIGINT;
    v_status   TEXT;
    v_phone_h  TEXT;
    v_bound_id BIGINT;
    c_chal_h   TEXT := repeat('a', 64);
    c_code_h   TEXT := repeat('b', 64);
    c_ph_hash  TEXT := repeat('c', 64);
BEGIN
    -- 1. Insert temporary parent auth_otp row
    INSERT INTO auth_otp (phone_hash, code_hash, purpose, expires_at)
    VALUES (c_ph_hash, c_code_h, 'login', now() + INTERVAL '5 minutes')
    RETURNING id INTO v_otp_id;

    -- 2. Call create_otp_challenge
    v_chal_id := create_otp_challenge(
        p_otp_id               => v_otp_id,
        p_challenge_token_hash => c_chal_h,
        p_ttl_seconds          => 180,
        p_purpose              => 'login'
    );
    RAISE NOTICE 'Challenge created with ID: %', v_chal_id;

    -- 3. Verify OTP challenge with matching code hash
    SELECT status, phone_hash, otp_id
      INTO v_status, v_phone_h, v_bound_id
      FROM verify_otp_challenge(c_chal_h, c_code_h, 'login');

    RAISE NOTICE 'Verification result: status=%, phone_hash=%, otp_id=%', v_status, v_phone_h, v_bound_id;

    IF v_status <> 'ok' OR v_phone_h <> c_ph_hash OR v_bound_id <> v_otp_id THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'Verification test failed! Got status=%', v_status;
    END IF;

    -- 4. Verify replay attempt fails with challenge_consumed
    SELECT status INTO v_status FROM verify_otp_challenge(c_chal_h, c_code_h, 'login');
    RAISE NOTICE 'Replay test result: status=%', v_status;

    IF v_status <> 'challenge_consumed' THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'Replay attack guard failed! Expected challenge_consumed, got %', v_status;
    END IF;

    -- 5. Cleanup test records
    DELETE FROM auth_otp WHERE id = v_otp_id;
    RAISE NOTICE 'Test passed successfully! Cleaned up test records.';
END;
$$;
```

## 6. Troubleshooting Common Issues

### Issue 1: `relation "auth_otp" does not exist`
- **Cause:** Your local PostgreSQL database was never seeded with the core database schema.
- **Fix:** Initialize your database using the master schema first:
  ```powershell
  psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5432 -U postgres -d volunteer_coordination_db -f postgres_sql\updated_volunteer_coordination_system_Database.sql
  ```

### Issue 2: `'psql' is not recognized as an internal or external command`
- **Cause:** PostgreSQL's `bin/` directory is not added to your system `PATH`.
- **Fix:** Use **Method A** (`.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/alter_local_db.py`), which uses the project's Python virtual environment and does not depend on system `PATH`.

### Issue 3: `password authentication failed for user "postgres"`
- **Cause:** Your local PostgreSQL password differs from the default (`postgres`).
- **Fix:** Set the environment variable before running:
  ```powershell
  $env:PGPASSWORD = "your_actual_password"
  .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/alter_local_db.py
  ```

### Issue 4: `could not connect to server: Connection refused`
- **Cause:** PostgreSQL service is not currently running.
- **Fix (Windows):** Check and start the service:
  ```powershell
  Get-Service postgresql*
  Start-Service postgresql-x64-16  # (or your installed version)
  ```

---

## 7. Rollback Procedure

If you ever need to revert the database back to the pre-v0.12.0 schema, execute the rollback script below:

```sql
BEGIN;

-- 1. Drop trigger and trigger guard function
DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_01_auth_otp_challenge_guard ON auth_otp_challenge;
DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS trg_auth_otp_challenge_before();

-- 2. Drop stored functions
DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS verify_otp_challenge(TEXT, TEXT, TEXT);
DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS create_otp_challenge(BIGINT, TEXT, INTEGER, TEXT, TEXT, TEXT);
DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS purge_expired_otp_challenges(INTERVAL);

-- 3. Drop table (cascades indexes and foreign keys)
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS auth_otp_challenge CASCADE;

COMMIT;
```

> [!NOTE]
> Because `auth_otp_challenge` references `auth_otp` with `ON DELETE CASCADE`, rolling back this migration only drops the challenge table and does **NOT** delete any existing user accounts, passwords, or active parent `auth_otp` rows.

# Database Migration Guide: v0.12.0 OTP Challenge & Session Handshake

**Document ID:** `DOC-MIG-v0.12.0-DB-UPGRADE`  
**Milestone Version:** `v0.12.0`  
**Phase:** Phase 1 (PostgreSQL OTP Challenge Schema, Stored Function & Key Separation)  
**Target Engine:** PostgreSQL 14+ (Database-First Architecture)  
**Schema Script Path:** `postgres_sql/v0_12_0_auth_otp_challenge_upgrade.sql`  
**Master Database Script:** `postgres_sql/updated_volunteer_coordination_system_Database.sql`  

---

## 1. Overview & Architectural Motivation

In Release v0.12.0, authentication transitions from the legacy protocol (which repeatedly re-transmitted raw phone numbers during verification) to a **tokenized, session-bound OTP challenge handshake**:

1. **Exact OTP Row Binding:** Rather than querying the latest unconsumed OTP by phone hash, verification is bound strictly to an exact `auth_otp` primary key record (`otp_id`).
2. **Dual Expiry Clocks:** Challenge TTL is capped at **180 seconds** (`min(now() + 180s, otp.expires_at)`). Both the challenge clock and the parent OTP clock are enforced by PostgreSQL.
3. **Deterministic Row Locking:** Verification locks the challenge row first, then locks the exact linked `auth_otp` row `FOR UPDATE` to eliminate concurrency race conditions.
4. **Single-Use Consumption:** Successful verification marks both the challenge and the parent OTP row as consumed simultaneously. Subsequent verify attempts fail immediately with `challenge_consumed`.
5. **No Raw Secrets in DB:** The database stores only `HMAC-SHA256(AUTH_SESSION_TOKEN_SECRET, raw_token)` in a 64-character column. The raw 256-bit challenge token is never persisted.

---

## 3. Detailed Schema Alterations

The migration performs the following additive operations:

### 3.1 New Table: `auth_otp_challenge`
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS auth_otp_challenge (
    id                   BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    otp_id               BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES auth_otp (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    challenge_token_hash TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    purpose              TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'login',
    created_at           TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    expires_at           TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    consumed_at          TIMESTAMPTZ,
    request_id           TEXT,
    identity_nonce_hash  TEXT,

    CONSTRAINT ck_auth_otp_challenge_purpose
        CHECK (purpose IN ('login', 'qr_registration')),
    CONSTRAINT ck_auth_otp_challenge_token_hash_len
        CHECK (length(challenge_token_hash) = 64),
    CONSTRAINT ck_auth_otp_challenge_expiry
        CHECK (expires_at > created_at),
    CONSTRAINT ck_auth_otp_challenge_consumed
        CHECK (consumed_at IS NULL OR consumed_at >= created_at)
);
```

### 3.2 Indexes Created
- `idx_auth_otp_challenge_otp_id`: Fast foreign key navigation and cascade operations.
- `idx_auth_otp_challenge_expires`: Partial index for rapid scanning of unconsumed, expiring challenges.
- `idx_auth_otp_challenge_nonce`: Unique partial index on `identity_nonce_hash` for replay attack prevention.

### 3.3 Integrity Trigger: `trg_01_auth_otp_challenge_guard`
A `BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE` trigger enforces two critical database invariants that standard SQL constraints cannot:
1. `NEW.expires_at <= v_otp.expires_at`: A challenge cannot outlive its parent OTP row.
2. `NEW.purpose == v_otp.purpose`: The challenge purpose must match the underlying OTP purpose.

### 3.4 Atomic Stored Procedure: `create_otp_challenge`
```sql
create_otp_challenge(
    p_otp_id               BIGINT,
    p_challenge_token_hash TEXT,
    p_ttl_seconds          INTEGER DEFAULT 180,
    p_purpose              TEXT DEFAULT 'login',
    p_request_id           TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
    p_identity_nonce_hash  TEXT DEFAULT NULL
) RETURNS BIGINT
```
- Automatically caps the TTL to `LEAST(p_ttl_seconds, 180)` and caps `expires_at` to `v_otp.expires_at`.
- Returns the new `auth_otp_challenge.id`.

### 3.5 Atomic Verification Stored Procedure: `verify_otp_challenge`
```sql
verify_otp_challenge(
    p_challenge_token_hash TEXT,
    p_code_hash            TEXT,
    p_purpose              TEXT DEFAULT 'login'
) RETURNS TABLE (
    status     TEXT,
    phone_hash TEXT,
    otp_id     BIGINT
)
```
- **Deterministic Row Locking:** Locks `auth_otp_challenge` first, then locks `auth_otp` with `FOR UPDATE`.
- **Status Returns:**
  - `'ok'` — Correct code; both challenge and OTP rows atomically consumed (`consumed_at = now()`); returns `phone_hash`.
  - `'invalid_challenge'` — Challenge not found or purpose mismatch.
  - `'challenge_consumed'` — Already consumed in a prior or concurrent verify attempt.
  - `'challenge_expired'` — Either challenge or parent OTP row has expired.
  - `'too_many_attempts'` — Parent OTP row reached `otp_max_attempts`.
  - `'invalid_code'` — Code hash does not match; increments `attempt_count` on the exact `auth_otp` row.

### 3.6 Data Retention & Cleanup Functions
- `purge_expired_otp_challenges(p_retention INTERVAL DEFAULT INTERVAL '1 day')`: Cleans up consumed or expired challenges older than the retention threshold. Active (unconsumed) challenges are never touched.
- `purge_expired_otps()`: Replaced to invoke challenge cleanup before purging expired parent OTPs.

---


/**
 * @format
 */

import {
  ApiClient,
  redactSensitiveData,
  RequestTelemetry,
  TransportAdapter,
} from '../src/core/api/apiClient';
import { setApiConfig } from '../src/core/api/apiConfig';
import { MemoryTokenStore } from '../src/core/auth/tokenStore';
import { SessionManager } from '../src/core/auth/sessionManager';

describe('ApiClient', () => {
  let memoryTokenStore: MemoryTokenStore;
  let sessionMgr: SessionManager;

  beforeEach(() => {
    setApiConfig({
      baseUrl: 'http://10.0.2.2:8000',
      apiPrefix: '/api/v1',
      defaultTimeoutMs: 5000,
    });
    memoryTokenStore = new MemoryTokenStore();
    sessionMgr = new SessionManager(memoryTokenStore);
  });

  it('joins base URL and /api/v1/ prefix cleanly for GET requests', async () => {
    let capturedUrl = '';
    const mockTransport: TransportAdapter = async (input) => {
      capturedUrl = input;
      return new Response(JSON.stringify({ results: [] }), {
        status: 200,
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      });
    };

    const client = new ApiClient(mockTransport, memoryTokenStore, sessionMgr);
    const result = await client.get('/events/');

    expect(result.ok).toBe(true);
    expect(capturedUrl).toBe('http://10.0.2.2:8000/api/v1/events/');
  });

  it('serializes query parameters including arrays and booleans', async () => {
    let capturedUrl = '';
    const mockTransport: TransportAdapter = async (input) => {
      capturedUrl = input;
      return new Response(JSON.stringify({ results: [] }), { status: 200 });
    };

    const client = new ApiClient(mockTransport, memoryTokenStore, sessionMgr);
    await client.get('/events/', {
      params: {
        starts_after: '2026-11-15T00:00:00Z',
        upcoming: true,
        charity_field: ['teaching', 'cooking'],
      },
    });

    expect(capturedUrl).toContain('starts_after=2026-11-15T00%3A00%3A00Z');
    expect(capturedUrl).toContain('upcoming=true');
    expect(capturedUrl).toContain('charity_field=teaching');
    expect(capturedUrl).toContain('charity_field=cooking');
  });

  it('injects "Authorization: Token <key>" header when token exists and authRequired !== false', async () => {
    await memoryTokenStore.setToken('auth-token-xyz-123');

    let capturedHeaders: Record<string, string> = {};
    const mockTransport: TransportAdapter = async (_, init) => {
      capturedHeaders = (init?.headers as Record<string, string>) || {};
      return new Response(JSON.stringify({ id: 1, displayName: 'Volunteer' }), {
        status: 200,
      });
    };

    const client = new ApiClient(mockTransport, memoryTokenStore, sessionMgr);
    const result = await client.get('/me/');

    expect(result.ok).toBe(true);
    expect(capturedHeaders.Authorization).toBe('Token auth-token-xyz-123');
  });

  it('omits Authorization header when authRequired: false even if token exists in TokenStore', async () => {
    await memoryTokenStore.setToken('secret-logged-in-token');

    let capturedHeaders: Record<string, string> = {};
    const mockTransport: TransportAdapter = async (_, init) => {
      capturedHeaders = (init?.headers as Record<string, string>) || {};
      return new Response(JSON.stringify({ status: 'queued' }), { status: 200 });
    };

    const client = new ApiClient(mockTransport, memoryTokenStore, sessionMgr);

  });

  it('handles HTTP 204 No Content without JSON parsing errors', async () => {

  it('DOES NOT clear token on HTTP 403 Forbidden or other errors', async () => {

  it('normalizes HTTP 400 domain errors correctly', async () => {

          err.name = 'AbortError';

  it('supports all standard HTTP verbs: POST, PATCH, PUT, DELETE', async () => {

    it('automatically generates an X-Request-ID correlation header when none is provided', async () => {
      let capturedHeaders: Record<string, string> = {};
      const mockTransport: TransportAdapter = async (_, init) => {
        capturedHeaders = (init?.headers as Record<string, string>) || {};
        return new Response(JSON.stringify({ ok: true }), { status: 200 });

      expect(capturedHeaders['X-Request-ID'].length).toBeGreaterThan(5);
    });

    it('preserves caller-supplied X-Request-ID correlation header', async () => {
      let capturedHeaders: Record<string, string> = {};
      const mockTransport: TransportAdapter = async (_, init) => {
        capturedHeaders = (init?.headers as Record<string, string>) || {};
        return new Response(JSON.stringify({ ok: true }), { status: 200 });
      };

      const client = new ApiClient(mockTransport, memoryTokenStore, sessionMgr);
      await client.get('/health/', {

      expect(capturedHeaders['X-Request-ID']).toBe('custom-trace-id-xyz-987');
    });

    it('emits structured request timing telemetry on successful completion', async () => {
      const recorded: RequestTelemetry[] = [];
      const mockTransport: TransportAdapter = async () => {
        return new Response(JSON.stringify({ results: [] }), { status: 200 });
      };

      const client = new ApiClient(mockTransport, memoryTokenStore, sessionMgr);
      const unsubscribe = client.onTelemetry(t => recorded.push(t));

      await client.get('/events/', {
        headers: { 'X-Request-ID': 'telemetry-test-001' },
      });

      expect(recorded.length).toBe(1);
      expect(recorded[0].requestId).toBe('telemetry-test-001');
      expect(recorded[0].method).toBe('GET');
      expect(recorded[0].url).toBe('http://10.0.2.2:8000/api/v1/events/');
      expect(recorded[0].status).toBe(200);
      expect(recorded[0].ok).toBe(true);
      expect(recorded[0].durationMs).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);

      unsubscribe();
      await client.get('/events/');
      expect(recorded.length).toBe(1); // Unsubscribed, no new telemetry recorded
    });

    it('emits structured request telemetry on error and timeout responses', async () => {
      const recorded: RequestTelemetry[] = [];
      const mockTransport: TransportAdapter = async () => {
        return new Response(
          JSON.stringify({ error: { code: 'not_found', message: 'Resource not found' } }),
          { status: 404 },
        );
      };

      const client = new ApiClient(mockTransport, memoryTokenStore, sessionMgr);
      client.onTelemetry(t => recorded.push(t));

      expect(recorded.length).toBe(1);
      expect(recorded[0].status).toBe(404);
      expect(recorded[0].ok).toBe(false);
      expect(recorded[0].errorCode).toBe('not_found');
    });

    it('redacts sensitive fields (Authorization, phone, otp, code, token, cit) recursively', () => {
      const payload = {
        authorization: 'Bearer secret-access-token',
        phone: '+959123456789',
        otp: '123456',
        code: '654321',
        token: 'drf-auth-token-111',
        auth_session_token: 'challenge-session-token-222',
        cit: 'client-identity-token-333',
        password: 'my-super-secret-password',
        display_name: 'Volunteer User',
        role: 'volunteer',
        meta: {
          phone: '+959987654321',
          safe_id: 42,
          nested: {
            auth_token: 'nested-token-value',
          },
        },
      };

      const redacted = redactSensitiveData(payload) as Record<string, unknown>;

      expect(redacted.authorization).toBe('[REDACTED]');
      expect(redacted.phone).toBe('[REDACTED]');
      expect(redacted.otp).toBe('[REDACTED]');
      expect(redacted.code).toBe('[REDACTED]');
      expect(redacted.token).toBe('[REDACTED]');
      expect(redacted.auth_session_token).toBe('[REDACTED]');
      expect(redacted.cit).toBe('[REDACTED]');
      expect(redacted.password).toBe('[REDACTED]');

      // Non-sensitive fields preserved
      expect(redacted.display_name).toBe('Volunteer User');
      expect(redacted.role).toBe('volunteer');

      // Nested fields correctly redacted
      const meta = redacted.meta as Record<string, unknown>;
      expect(meta.phone).toBe('[REDACTED]');
      expect(meta.safe_id).toBe(42);
      const nested = meta.nested as Record<string, unknown>;
      expect(nested.auth_token).toBe('[REDACTED]');
    });

    it('cleans up caller AbortSignal event listener on success exit path', async () => {
      const controller = new AbortController();
      let listenerCount = 0;

      const mockTransport: TransportAdapter = async () => {
        return new Response(JSON.stringify({ success: true }), { status: 200 });
      };

      const originalAdd = controller.signal.addEventListener.bind(controller.signal);
      const originalRemove = controller.signal.removeEventListener.bind(controller.signal);

      jest.spyOn(controller.signal, 'addEventListener').mockImplementation((type, listener, options) => {
        if (type === 'abort') {
          listenerCount++;
        }
        return originalAdd(type, listener, options);
      });

      jest.spyOn(controller.signal, 'removeEventListener').mockImplementation((type, listener, options) => {
        if (type === 'abort') {
          listenerCount--;
        }
        return originalRemove(type, listener, options);
      });

      const client = new ApiClient(mockTransport, memoryTokenStore, sessionMgr);
      await client.get('/events/', { signal: controller.signal });

      expect(listenerCount).toBe(0);
    });

    it('cleans up caller AbortSignal event listener on error/exception exit path', async () => {
      const controller = new AbortController();
      let listenerCount = 0;

      const mockTransport: TransportAdapter = async () => {
        throw new Error('Socket abruptly disconnected');
      };

      const originalAdd = controller.signal.addEventListener.bind(controller.signal);
      const originalRemove = controller.signal.removeEventListener.bind(controller.signal);

      jest.spyOn(controller.signal, 'addEventListener').mockImplementation((type, listener, options) => {
        if (type === 'abort') {
          listenerCount++;
        }
        return originalAdd(type, listener, options);
      });

      jest.spyOn(controller.signal, 'removeEventListener').mockImplementation((type, listener, options) => {
        if (type === 'abort') {
          listenerCount--;
        }
        return originalRemove(type, listener, options);
      });

      const client = new ApiClient(mockTransport, memoryTokenStore, sessionMgr);
      await client.get('/events/', { signal: controller.signal });

      expect(listenerCount).toBe(0);
    });

    it('aborts request when caller AbortSignal fires during execution', async () => {
      const callerController = new AbortController();

      const mockTransport: TransportAdapter = async (_, init) => {
        if (init?.signal?.aborted) {
          const err = new Error('The user aborted a request.');
          err.name = 'AbortError';
          throw err;
        }
        return new Promise((_, reject) => {
          init?.signal?.addEventListener('abort', () => {
            const err = new Error('The user aborted a request.');
            err.name = 'AbortError';
            reject(err);
          });
        });
      };

      const client = new ApiClient(mockTransport, memoryTokenStore, sessionMgr);
      const promise = client.get('/slow/', { signal: callerController.signal });

      // Trigger caller abort
      callerController.abort();

      const result = await promise;
      expect(result.ok).toBe(false);
      if (!result.ok) {
        expect(result.error.kind).toBe('network');
      }
    });

    it('forwards explicit Idempotency-Key headers without automatic POST retry', async () => {
      let callCount = 0;
      let capturedHeaders: Record<string, string> = {};

      const mockTransport: TransportAdapter = async (_, init) => {
        callCount++;
        capturedHeaders = (init?.headers as Record<string, string>) || {};
        return new Response(
          JSON.stringify({ error: { code: 'server_error', message: 'Temporary glitch' } }),
          { status: 500 },
        );
      };

      const client = new ApiClient(mockTransport, memoryTokenStore, sessionMgr);
      const result = await client.post(
        '/checkin/attendance/manual-checkin/',
        { event_id: 1, user_id: 2 },
        { headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': 'idempotent-key-uuid-1234' } },
      );

      expect(result.ok).toBe(false);
      expect(capturedHeaders['Idempotency-Key']).toBe('idempotent-key-uuid-1234');
      // STRICT INVARIANT: Non-idempotent/POST mutations are NEVER automatically retried
      expect(callCount).toBe(1);
    });
  });
});

/**

import { PermissionsAndroid, Platform } from 'react-native';
import {
  defaultLocationProvider,
  defaultMockLocationProvider,
  defaultNativeLocationProvider,
  MockLocationProvider,
  NativeDeviceLocationProvider,
} from '../src/core/location/locationProvider';
import {
  AUTH_TOKEN_STORAGE_KEY,
  MemoryTokenStore,
  PluggableTokenStore,
} from '../src/core/auth/tokenStore';
import {
  resetDataMode,
  setDataMode,
} from '../src/app/configuration/dataMode';
import type { OtpRequestResponseDto } from '../src/data/dto/authDto';

describe('Phase 6: LocationProvider & Android Permissions (P0-07)', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    resetDataMode();
    jest.clearAllMocks();
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    resetDataMode();
    jest.restoreAllMocks();
  });

  describe('MockLocationProvider', () => {
    it('returns default Yangon demo coordinates in mock mode', async () => {
      const mockProvider = new MockLocationProvider();
      const permission = await mockProvider.requestPermission();
      expect(permission).toBe('granted');

      const fix = await mockProvider.getCurrentPosition();
      expect(fix.latitude).toBe(16.805);
      expect(fix.longitude).toBe(96.155);
      expect(fix.accuracyM).toBe(15);
      expect(fix.isMocked).toBe(true);
      expect(new Date(fix.capturedAt).getTime()).not.toBeNaN();
    });

    it('allows updating mock fix dynamically', async () => {
      const mockProvider = new MockLocationProvider();
      mockProvider.setMockFix({
        latitude: 16.820,
        longitude: 96.130,
        accuracyM: 8,
      });

      const fix = await mockProvider.getCurrentPosition();
      expect(fix.latitude).toBe(16.820);
      expect(fix.longitude).toBe(96.130);
      expect(fix.accuracyM).toBe(8);
    });

    it('throws when permission state is set to denied or unavailable', async () => {
      const mockProvider = new MockLocationProvider();
      mockProvider.setPermissionState('denied');
      expect(await mockProvider.requestPermission()).toBe('denied');
      await expect(mockProvider.getCurrentPosition()).rejects.toThrow(
        'Location permission denied.',
      );

      mockProvider.setPermissionState('unavailable');
      expect(await mockProvider.requestPermission()).toBe('unavailable');
      await expect(mockProvider.getCurrentPosition()).rejects.toThrow(
        'Device location services are unavailable.',
      );
    });
  });

  describe('NativeDeviceLocationProvider', () => {
    it('requests Android ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION and ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION permissions', async () => {
      const originalOS = Platform.OS;
      (Platform as any).OS = 'android';

      const checkSpy = jest
        .spyOn(PermissionsAndroid, 'check')
        .mockResolvedValueOnce(false);
      const requestMultipleSpy = jest
        .spyOn(PermissionsAndroid, 'requestMultiple')
        .mockResolvedValueOnce({
          'android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION': PermissionsAndroid.RESULTS.GRANTED,
          'android.permission.ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION': PermissionsAndroid.RESULTS.GRANTED,
        } as any);

      const provider = new NativeDeviceLocationProvider();
      const permission = await provider.requestPermission();

      expect(permission).toBe('granted');
      expect(checkSpy).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
        'android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION',
      );
      expect(requestMultipleSpy).toHaveBeenCalledWith([
        'android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION',
        'android.permission.ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION',
      ]);

      (Platform as any).OS = originalOS;
    });

    it('returns denied when Android permissions are rejected', async () => {
      const originalOS = Platform.OS;
      (Platform as any).OS = 'android';

      jest.spyOn(PermissionsAndroid, 'check').mockResolvedValueOnce(false);
      jest.spyOn(PermissionsAndroid, 'requestMultiple').mockResolvedValueOnce({
        'android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION': PermissionsAndroid.RESULTS.DENIED,
        'android.permission.ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION': PermissionsAndroid.RESULTS.DENIED,
      } as any);

      const provider = new NativeDeviceLocationProvider();
      const permission = await provider.requestPermission();

      expect(permission).toBe('denied');

      (Platform as any).OS = originalOS;
    });

    it('fails fast without calling GPS hardware if permission is denied', async () => {
      const provider = new NativeDeviceLocationProvider();
      jest.spyOn(provider, 'requestPermission').mockResolvedValueOnce('denied');

      const mockGeo = { getCurrentPosition: jest.fn() };
      provider.setCustomGeolocationModule(mockGeo);

      await expect(provider.getCurrentPosition()).rejects.toThrow(
        'Location permission denied. Cannot capture device GPS telemetry.',
      );
      expect(mockGeo.getCurrentPosition).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    });

    it('captures and formats device GPS fix when permission is granted', async () => {
      const provider = new NativeDeviceLocationProvider();
      jest.spyOn(provider, 'requestPermission').mockResolvedValueOnce('granted');

      const mockGeo = {
        getCurrentPosition: jest.fn((success) => {
          success({
            coords: {
              latitude: 16.799,
              longitude: 96.162,
              accuracy: 12.5,
            },
            timestamp: 1731800000000,
            mocked: false,
          });
        }),
      };
      provider.setCustomGeolocationModule(mockGeo);

      const fix = await provider.getCurrentPosition();
      expect(fix.latitude).toBe(16.799);
      expect(fix.longitude).toBe(96.162);
      expect(fix.accuracyM).toBe(12.5);
      expect(fix.isMocked).toBe(false);
      expect(fix.capturedAt).toBe(new Date(1731800000000).toISOString());
    });
  });

  describe('defaultLocationProvider Mode Branching', () => {
    it('branches to MockLocationProvider when dataMode is mock', async () => {
      setDataMode('mock');
      const fix = await defaultLocationProvider.getCurrentPosition();
      expect(fix.isMocked).toBe(true);
      expect(fix.latitude).toBe(16.805);
    });

    it('branches to NativeDeviceLocationProvider when dataMode is http', async () => {
      setDataMode('http');
      jest
        .spyOn(defaultNativeLocationProvider, 'requestPermission')
        .mockResolvedValueOnce('denied');

      await expect(defaultLocationProvider.getCurrentPosition()).rejects.toThrow(
        'Location permission denied. Cannot capture device GPS telemetry.',
      );
    });
  });
});

describe('Phase 6: Secure Token Persistence & PluggableTokenStore (P0-08)', () => {
  it('falls back seamlessly to MemoryTokenStore in test environments', async () => {
    const memory = new MemoryTokenStore();
    const store = new PluggableTokenStore(memory);

    const tier = await store.getStorageTier();
    expect(tier).toBe('memory');

    await store.setToken('secret-test-token-1234');
    const stored = await store.getToken();
    expect(stored).toBe('secret-test-token-1234');

    await store.clearToken();
    expect(await store.getToken()).toBeNull();
  });

  it('allows injecting a custom secure storage driver and takes precedence', async () => {
    const custom = new MemoryTokenStore('initial-preloaded-token');
    const store = new PluggableTokenStore();
    store.setCustomStorage(custom);

    expect(await store.getStorageTier()).toBe('custom');
    expect(await store.getToken()).toBe('initial-preloaded-token');

    await store.setToken('updated-secure-token');
    expect(await custom.getToken()).toBe('updated-secure-token');
    expect(await store.getToken()).toBe('updated-secure-token');

    await store.clearToken();
    expect(await custom.getToken()).toBeNull();
  });

  it('trims whitespace and rejects empty tokens safely', async () => {
    const store = new PluggableTokenStore(new MemoryTokenStore());
    await store.setToken('   token-with-whitespace   ');
    expect(await store.getToken()).toBe('token-with-whitespace');
  });

  it('guarantees zero token leakage in diagnostics', async () => {
    const store = new PluggableTokenStore(new MemoryTokenStore());
    await store.setToken('super-confidential-auth-token-xyz');

    const tier = await store.getStorageTier();
    // Tier diagnostics must only expose the storage kind, never token content
    expect(tier).toBe('memory');
    expect(JSON.stringify(tier)).not.toContain('super-confidential');
  });
});

describe('Phase 6: Truthful OTP Delivery Status (P0-09)', () => {
  it('correctly maps truthful delivery status and channel in OtpRequestResponseDto', () => {
    const responseSent: OtpRequestResponseDto = {
      status: 'sent',
      delivery: {
        delivered: true,
        channel: 'sms',
        provider_configured: true,
      },
    };

    expect(responseSent.status).toBe('sent');
    expect(responseSent.delivery?.delivered).toBe(true);
    expect(responseSent.delivery?.channel).toBe('sms');

    const responseConsole: OtpRequestResponseDto = {
      status: 'dev_console',
      delivery: {
        delivered: true,
        channel: 'console',
        method: 'console',
        provider_configured: true,
      },
      dev_code: '1234',
    };

    expect(responseConsole.status).toBe('dev_console');
    expect(responseConsole.delivery?.delivered).toBe(true);
    expect(responseConsole.delivery?.channel).toBe('console');
    expect(responseConsole.dev_code).toBe('1234');

    const responsePending: OtpRequestResponseDto = {
      status: 'pending_provider',
      delivery: {
        delivered: false,
        channel: 'console',
        provider_configured: false,
      },
    };

    expect(responsePending.status).toBe('pending_provider');
    expect(responsePending.delivery?.delivered).toBe(false);
  });
});

} from '../src/core/auth/tokenStore';
import { SessionManager } from '../src/core/auth/sessionManager';

describe('TokenStore & SessionManager', () => {
  describe('MemoryTokenStore (Injected Test Store)', () => {
    it('sets, retrieves, and clears token in memory', async () => {
      const store = new MemoryTokenStore();
      expect(await store.getToken()).toBeNull();

      await store.setToken('test-drf-token-12345');
      expect(await store.getToken()).toBe('test-drf-token-12345');

      await store.clearToken();
      expect(await store.getToken()).toBeNull();
    });

    it('trims whitespace when storing token', async () => {
      const store = new MemoryTokenStore();
      await store.setToken('   abc123token   ');
      expect(await store.getToken()).toBe('abc123token');
    });

    it('supports preloading an initial token via constructor', async () => {
      const store = new MemoryTokenStore('  preloaded-token  ');
      expect(await store.getToken()).toBe('preloaded-token');
    });
  });

  describe('KeychainTokenStore (Declared Secure Storage)', () => {
    it('confirms defaultTokenStore defaults to Keychain hardware storage tier', async () => {
      expect(await defaultTokenStore.getStorageTier()).toBe('keychain');
    });

    it('isolates authentication token storage key from theme preference key', () => {
      expect(AUTH_TOKEN_STORAGE_KEY).toBe('@volunteer_mgmt:auth_token');
      expect(AUTH_TOKEN_STORAGE_KEY).not.toBe('@volunteer_mgmt:theme_preference');
    });

    it('successfully persists, retrieves, and clears token when Keychain is available', async () => {
      const mockStorage = new Map<string, string>();
      const mockKeychain = {
        setGenericPassword: jest.fn(async (username: string, password: string, options?: { service?: string }) => {
          const service = options?.service || AUTH_TOKEN_STORAGE_KEY;
          mockStorage.set(service, password);
          return true;
        }),
        getGenericPassword: jest.fn(async (options?: { service?: string }) => {
          const service = options?.service || AUTH_TOKEN_STORAGE_KEY;
          const password = mockStorage.get(service);
          return password ? { username: 'auth_token', password, service } : false;
        }),
        resetGenericPassword: jest.fn(async (options?: { service?: string }) => {
          const service = options?.service || AUTH_TOKEN_STORAGE_KEY;
          mockStorage.delete(service);
          return true;
        }),
      };

      const store = new KeychainTokenStore();
      (store as unknown as { getKeychain: () => unknown }).getKeychain = () => mockKeychain;

      expect(store.isAvailable()).toBe(true);

      // Initially null
      expect(await store.getToken()).toBeNull();

      // Persist
      await store.setToken('secure-hardware-token-001');
      expect(mockKeychain.setGenericPassword).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
        'auth_token',
        'secure-hardware-token-001',
        { service: AUTH_TOKEN_STORAGE_KEY },
      );
      expect(await store.getToken()).toBe('secure-hardware-token-001');

      // Clear
      await store.clearToken();
      expect(mockKeychain.resetGenericPassword).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
        service: AUTH_TOKEN_STORAGE_KEY,
      });
      expect(await store.getToken()).toBeNull();
    });

    it('clears token when setToken is called with an empty string', async () => {
      const store = new KeychainTokenStore();
      const clearSpy = jest.spyOn(store, 'clearToken').mockResolvedValue(undefined);

      await store.setToken('   ');
      expect(clearSpy).toHaveBeenCalled();
    });

    it('FAIL-CLOSED: throws SessionStorageError when Keychain is unavailable', async () => {
      const store = new KeychainTokenStore();
      (store as unknown as { getKeychain: () => unknown }).getKeychain = () => null;

      expect(store.isAvailable()).toBe(false);

      await expect(store.getToken()).rejects.toThrow(SessionStorageError);
      await expect(store.getToken()).rejects.toThrow(/unavailable/i);

      await expect(store.setToken('token-fail')).rejects.toThrow(SessionStorageError);
      await expect(store.clearToken()).rejects.toThrow(SessionStorageError);
    });

    it('FAIL-CLOSED: throws SessionStorageError when setGenericPassword returns false (rejected write)', async () => {
      const mockKeychain = {
        setGenericPassword: jest.fn(async () => false),
        getGenericPassword: jest.fn(async () => false),
        resetGenericPassword: jest.fn(async () => true),
      };

      const store = new KeychainTokenStore();
      (store as unknown as { getKeychain: () => unknown }).getKeychain = () => mockKeychain;

      await expect(store.setToken('rejected-token')).rejects.toThrow(SessionStorageError);
      try {
        await store.setToken('rejected-token');
      } catch (err) {
        expect(err).toBeInstanceOf(SessionStorageError);
        expect((err as SessionStorageError).code).toBe('SECURE_STORAGE_WRITE_REJECTED');
      }
    });

    it('FAIL-CLOSED: wraps driver native exceptions in SessionStorageError', async () => {
      const mockKeychain = {
        setGenericPassword: jest.fn(async () => {
          throw new Error('Keystore corrupted or locked');
        }),
        getGenericPassword: jest.fn(async () => {
          throw new Error('Keymaster communication fault');
        }),
        resetGenericPassword: jest.fn(async () => {
          throw new Error('Keychain item removal failed');
        }),
      };

      const store = new KeychainTokenStore();
      (store as unknown as { getKeychain: () => unknown }).getKeychain = () => mockKeychain;

      await expect(store.setToken('crash-token')).rejects.toThrow(SessionStorageError);
      try {
        await store.setToken('crash-token');
      } catch (err) {
        expect((err as SessionStorageError).code).toBe('SECURE_STORAGE_WRITE_ERROR');
      }

      await expect(store.getToken()).rejects.toThrow(SessionStorageError);
      try {
        await store.getToken();
      } catch (err) {
        expect((err as SessionStorageError).code).toBe('SECURE_STORAGE_READ_ERROR');
      }

      await expect(store.clearToken()).rejects.toThrow(SessionStorageError);
      try {
        await store.clearToken();
      } catch (err) {
        expect((err as SessionStorageError).code).toBe('SECURE_STORAGE_CLEAR_ERROR');
      }
    });
  });

  describe('Storage Capability Status & Diagnostics', () => {
    it('returns memory tier for MemoryTokenStore without leaking token values', () => {
      const memory = new MemoryTokenStore('secret-confidential-token-999');
      const status = getStorageCapabilityStatus(memory);

      expect(status.tier).toBe('memory');
      expect(status.isSecure).toBe(false);
      expect(status.isAvailable).toBe(true);

      const serialized = JSON.stringify(status);
      expect(serialized).not.toContain('secret-confidential');
    });

    it('returns keychain tier for KeychainTokenStore without leaking token values', () => {
      const status = getStorageCapabilityStatus(defaultTokenStore);
      expect(status.tier).toBe('keychain');
      expect(status.isSecure).toBe(true);
      expect(typeof status.isAvailable).toBe('boolean');
    });
  });

  describe('PluggableTokenStore Delegation', () => {
    it('uses custom storage backend when set', async () => {
      const memory = new MemoryTokenStore();
      const pluggable = new PluggableTokenStore();
      pluggable.setCustomStorage(memory);

      expect(await pluggable.getStorageTier()).toBe('custom');
      await pluggable.setToken('custom-token-xyz');
      expect(await pluggable.getToken()).toBe('custom-token-xyz');
      expect(await memory.getToken()).toBe('custom-token-xyz');

      await pluggable.clearToken();
      expect(await pluggable.getToken()).toBeNull();
      expect(await memory.getToken()).toBeNull();
    });

    it('uses explicitly injected fallback when provided', async () => {
      const memory = new MemoryTokenStore('fallback-token-456');
      const pluggable = new PluggableTokenStore(memory);

      expect(await pluggable.getStorageTier()).toBe('memory');
      expect(await pluggable.getToken()).toBe('fallback-token-456');

      await pluggable.setToken('updated-token');
      expect(await pluggable.getToken()).toBe('updated-token');
      expect(await memory.getToken()).toBe('updated-token');

      await pluggable.clearToken();
      expect(await pluggable.getToken()).toBeNull();
    });

    it('delegates to KeychainTokenStore when no custom storage or fallback is set', async () => {
      const pluggable = new PluggableTokenStore();
      expect(await pluggable.getStorageTier()).toBe('keychain');
    });
  });

  describe('SessionManager Lifecycle and Invariants', () => {
    let memoryStore: MemoryTokenStore;
    let sessionMgr: SessionManager;

    beforeEach(() => {
      memoryStore = new MemoryTokenStore();
      sessionMgr = new SessionManager(memoryStore);
    });

    it('correctly tracks authentication status with hasValidToken', async () => {
      expect(await sessionMgr.hasValidToken()).toBe(false);

      await sessionMgr.setToken('valid-token-777');
      expect(await sessionMgr.hasValidToken()).toBe(true);
      expect(await sessionMgr.getToken()).toBe('valid-token-777');

      await sessionMgr.logout();
      expect(await sessionMgr.hasValidToken()).toBe(false);
      expect(await sessionMgr.getToken()).toBeNull();
    });

    it('returns false for hasValidToken when token is only whitespace or empty', async () => {
      await sessionMgr.setToken('');
      expect(await sessionMgr.hasValidToken()).toBe(false);

      await sessionMgr.setToken('   ');
      expect(await sessionMgr.hasValidToken()).toBe(false);
    });

    it('fails closed: hasValidToken returns false when storage throws SessionStorageError', async () => {
      const brokenStore = new MemoryTokenStore();
      brokenStore.getToken = async () => {
        throw new SessionStorageError('Keystore unavailable', 'SECURE_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE');
      };

      const manager = new SessionManager(brokenStore);
      expect(await manager.hasValidToken()).toBe(false);
    });

    it('invokes onUnauthorized listener ONLY when handleUnauthorized is called (HTTP 401)', async () => {
      await sessionMgr.setToken('session-token-999');

      let unauthorizedTriggered = false;
      const unsubscribe = sessionMgr.onUnauthorized(() => {
        unauthorizedTriggered = true;
      });

      await sessionMgr.handleUnauthorized();

      expect(unauthorizedTriggered).toBe(true);
      expect(await sessionMgr.getToken()).toBeNull();
      expect(await sessionMgr.hasValidToken()).toBe(false);

      unsubscribe();
    });

    it('allows unsubscribing from onUnauthorized callback', async () => {
      let callCount = 0;
      const unsubscribe = sessionMgr.onUnauthorized(() => {
        callCount++;
      });

      await sessionMgr.handleUnauthorized();
      expect(callCount).toBe(1);

      unsubscribe();

      await sessionMgr.handleUnauthorized();
      expect(callCount).toBe(1);
    });

    it('handles listener exceptions gracefully without aborting subsequent listeners', async () => {
      let secondListenerFired = false;
      sessionMgr.onUnauthorized(() => {
        throw new Error('Faulty listener');
      });
      sessionMgr.onUnauthorized(() => {
        secondListenerFired = true;
      });

      await expect(sessionMgr.handleUnauthorized()).resolves.toBeUndefined();
      expect(secondListenerFired).toBe(true);
    });

    it('CRITICAL INVARIANT: token is preserved on non-401 scenarios', async () => {
      await sessionMgr.setToken('secure-user-token');

      // Simulating what happens during 403, 404, 409, 429, 500, network/timeout errors:
      // handleUnauthorized is NOT called
      expect(await sessionMgr.getToken()).toBe('secure-user-token');
      expect(await sessionMgr.hasValidToken()).toBe(true);
    });

    it('allows dynamically swapping the TokenStore via setTokenStore', async () => {
      const anotherStore = new MemoryTokenStore('swapped-token-111');
      sessionMgr.setTokenStore(anotherStore);

      expect(await sessionMgr.getToken()).toBe('swapped-token-111');
      expect(await sessionMgr.hasValidToken()).toBe(true);
    });
  });
});

      expect(capturedContext?.currentUser.email).toBeUndefined();
      expect(capturedContext?.currentUser.email).not.toBe('+959888777666');
