         WHERE id = NEW.event_id AND deleted_at IS NULL;
        IF NOT FOUND THEN
            RAISE EXCEPTION 'invalid_state: the event is already deleted';
        END IF;
    ELSIF NEW.action_type = 'event_restore' THEN
        UPDATE events SET deleted_at = NULL, deleted_by_id = NULL
         WHERE id = NEW.event_id AND deleted_at IS NOT NULL;
        IF NOT FOUND THEN
            RAISE EXCEPTION 'invalid_state: the event is not deleted';
        END IF;
    ELSIF NEW.action_type = 'event_cancel' THEN
        UPDATE events SET status = 'cancelled', cancel_reason = NEW.reason
         WHERE id = NEW.event_id AND status IN ('draft', 'published', 'active') AND deleted_at IS NULL;
        IF NOT FOUND THEN
            RAISE EXCEPTION 'invalid_state: only open, undeleted events can be cancelled';
        END IF;
    ELSIF NEW.action_type = 'feedback_hide' THEN
        UPDATE feedback SET status = 'hidden'
         WHERE id = NEW.feedback_id AND status = 'active';
        IF NOT FOUND THEN
            RAISE EXCEPTION 'invalid_state: the feedback is not active';
        END IF;
    END IF;

    PERFORM set_config('app.privileged_write', 'off', true);
    RETURN NULL;
END;
$$;

DO $$
DECLARE
    t TEXT;
BEGIN
    FOREACH t IN ARRAY ARRAY[
        'users', 'coordinator_profiles', 'user_verification_images', 'events',
        'event_posts', 'event_applications', 'assignments', 'attendance']
    LOOP
        EXECUTE format(
            'CREATE TRIGGER trg_90_%1$s_updated_at BEFORE UPDATE ON %1$I
             FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION set_updated_at()', t);
    END LOOP;
END;
$$;

-- =============================================================================
-- 20. VIEWS (11 Operational, Public & Admin Views)
-- =============================================================================

-- 20.1 Remaining places per post
CREATE VIEW v_event_post_capacity AS
SELECT p.id AS post_id,
       p.event_id,
       p.title,
       p.status,
       p.required_headcount,
       COUNT(a.id) AS assigned_count,
       GREATEST(p.required_headcount - COUNT(a.id), 0) AS remaining
  FROM event_posts p
  LEFT JOIN assignments a
         ON a.post_id = p.id AND a.status <> 'cancelled'
 GROUP BY p.id;

-- 20.2 What volunteers browse: published or active, not deleted
CREATE VIEW v_public_events AS
SELECT e.id AS event_id,
       e.title,
       e.description,
       e.purpose_type,
       e.location_name,
       e.landmark_text,
       e.latitude,
       e.longitude,
       e.geo_radius_m,
       e.geo_checkin_enabled,
       e.map_provider,
       e.start_at,
       e.end_at,
       e.application_deadline,
       e.status,
       e.acceptance_mode,
       e.max_participants,
       e.meals_provided,
       e.lodging_provided,
       e.travel_support_provided,
       e.compensation_kind,
       e.current_coordinator_id,
       cu.display_name AS coordinator_name,
       COALESCE((SELECT array_agg(f.field_code ORDER BY f.field_code)
                   FROM event_charity_fields f WHERE f.event_id = e.id), '{}'::TEXT[]) AS charity_fields,
       COALESCE((SELECT sum(c.remaining)
                   FROM v_event_post_capacity c
                  WHERE c.event_id = e.id AND c.status <> 'closed'), 0) AS spots_remaining
  FROM events e
  JOIN users cu ON cu.id = e.current_coordinator_id
 WHERE e.deleted_at IS NULL
   AND e.status IN ('published', 'active');

-- 20.3 Per-event counters for the coordinator board (subqueries avoid join fan-out)
CREATE VIEW v_event_summary AS
SELECT e.id AS event_id,
       e.title,
       e.status,
       e.owner_id,
       e.current_coordinator_id,
       e.start_at,
       e.end_at,
       e.acceptance_mode,
       e.auto_assign_enabled,
       e.max_participants,
       e.geo_checkin_enabled,
       e.map_provider,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM event_applications x WHERE x.event_id = e.id AND x.status = 'pending')    AS pending_count,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM event_applications x WHERE x.event_id = e.id AND x.status = 'accepted')   AS accepted_count,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM event_applications x WHERE x.event_id = e.id AND x.status = 'waitlisted') AS waitlisted_count,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM assignments x WHERE x.event_id = e.id AND x.status <> 'cancelled')        AS assignment_count,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM attendance x WHERE x.event_id = e.id AND x.status IN ('checked_in', 'completed')) AS checked_in_count,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM attendance x WHERE x.event_id = e.id AND x.confirmation_status = 'pending')       AS pending_confirmations
  FROM events e
 WHERE e.deleted_at IS NULL;

-- 20.4 Accepted applications that still have no assignment
CREATE VIEW v_accepted_unassigned AS
SELECT ap.id AS application_id,
       ap.event_id,
       ap.user_id,
       u.display_name,
       u.skills,
       u.physical_ok,
       u.can_lift_heavy,
       u.has_leader_experience,
       u.new_to_volunteer
  FROM event_applications ap
  JOIN users  u ON u.id = ap.user_id
  JOIN events e ON e.id = ap.event_id AND e.deleted_at IS NULL
 WHERE ap.status = 'accepted'
   AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM assignments a
                    WHERE a.application_id = ap.id AND a.status <> 'cancelled');

-- 20.5 Worker list with live check-in state
CREATE VIEW v_event_checkin_board AS
SELECT a.event_id,
       a.id AS assignment_id,
       u.id AS user_id,
       u.display_name,
       a.post_id,
       ep.title AS post_title,
       a.group_code,
       a.is_group_leader,
       a.status AS assignment_status,
       t.id AS attendance_id,
       t.status AS attendance_status,
       t.method,
       t.walk_in_flag,
       t.checkin_at,
       t.checkin_distance_m,
       t.confirmation_status
  FROM assignments a
  JOIN users u ON u.id = a.user_id
  LEFT JOIN event_posts ep ON ep.id = a.post_id
  LEFT JOIN attendance t ON t.event_id = a.event_id AND t.user_id = a.user_id
 WHERE a.status <> 'cancelled';

-- 20.6 Alias view for check-in status compatibility
CREATE VIEW v_event_checkin_status AS
SELECT event_id,
       user_id,
       display_name,
       post_id,
       post_title,
       group_code,
       is_group_leader,
       COALESCE(attendance_status, 'expected') AS attendance_status,
       checkin_at,
       method AS checkin_method,
       walk_in_flag,
       confirmation_status,
       checkin_distance_m
  FROM v_event_checkin_board;

-- 20.7 The coordinator's queue of geo check-ins waiting for a decision
CREATE VIEW v_pending_confirmations AS
SELECT t.id AS attendance_id,
       t.event_id,
       e.title AS event_title,
       e.owner_id,
       e.current_coordinator_id,
       t.user_id,
       u.display_name AS volunteer_name,
       t.checkin_at,
       t.checkin_latitude,
       t.checkin_longitude,
       t.checkin_accuracy_m,
       t.checkin_distance_m
  FROM attendance t
  JOIN events e ON e.id = t.event_id AND e.deleted_at IS NULL
  JOIN users  u ON u.id = t.user_id
 WHERE t.confirmation_status = 'pending';

-- 20.8 Geo check-in attempt log (for fraud & telemetry review)
CREATE VIEW v_geo_attempts_review AS
SELECT ga.id,
       ga.event_id,
       e.title AS event_title,
       ga.user_id,
       u.display_name,
       ga.attempted_at,
       ga.result,
       ga.distance_m,
       ga.radius_m,
       ga.accuracy_m,
       ga.device_mocked,
       ga.review_status,
       ga.reviewed_by_user_id,
       ga.reviewed_at,
       ga.review_note
  FROM attendance_geo_attempts ga
  JOIN events e ON e.id = ga.event_id
  JOIN users  u ON u.id = ga.user_id
 ORDER BY ga.attempted_at DESC;

-- 20.9 Coordinator handover history
CREATE VIEW v_event_coordinator_history AS
SELECT h.event_id,
       e.title AS event_title,
       h.from_coordinator_id,
       fu.display_name AS from_name,
       h.to_coordinator_id,
       tu.display_name AS to_name,
       h.changed_by_user_id,
       cu.display_name AS changed_by_name,
       h.reason,
       h.changed_at
  FROM event_coordinator_history h
  JOIN events e  ON e.id  = h.event_id
  LEFT JOIN users fu ON fu.id = h.from_coordinator_id
  JOIN users tu  ON tu.id = h.to_coordinator_id
  LEFT JOIN users cu ON cu.id = h.changed_by_user_id
 ORDER BY h.changed_at DESC;

-- 20.10 Per-user moderation summary
CREATE VIEW v_user_moderation_summary AS
SELECT m.target_user_id AS user_id,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE m.action_type = 'user_warning')  AS warning_count,
       max(m.created_at) FILTER (WHERE m.action_type = 'user_warning') AS last_warning_at,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE m.action_type = 'user_block')    AS block_count,
       max(m.created_at) FILTER (WHERE m.action_type = 'user_block')   AS last_block_at
  FROM moderation_actions m
 WHERE m.target_user_id IS NOT NULL
 GROUP BY m.target_user_id;

-- 20.11 Admin dashboard (one row)
CREATE VIEW v_admin_dashboard AS
SELECT
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE account_status = 'active')   AS active_users,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE account_status = 'blocked')  AS blocked_users,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE verification_status = 'pending') AS users_pending_verification,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_verification_images WHERE status = 'pending' AND is_current) AS images_pending_review,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM coordinator_profiles WHERE status = 'pending')  AS coordinators_pending_approval,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM coordinator_profiles WHERE status = 'approved') AS coordinators_approved,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND status = 'draft')     AS events_draft,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND status = 'published') AS events_published,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND status = 'active')    AS events_active,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND status = 'completed') AS events_completed,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND status = 'cancelled') AS events_cancelled,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL) AS events_deleted,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM attendance WHERE confirmation_status = 'pending') AS pending_checkin_confirmations,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM moderation_actions
      WHERE action_type = 'user_warning' AND created_at > now() - INTERVAL '30 days') AS warnings_last_30d;

-- =============================================================================
-- 21. SELF-TEST SUITE (Zero-Pollution Verification)
--     Run `SELECT * FROM self_test();` after loading to verify constraints,
--     triggers, composite FKs, EXCLUDE rules, and audit immutability.
--     All temporary rows (including audit_logs) are rolled back automatically.
-- =============================================================================

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION self_test()
RETURNS TABLE (test_name TEXT, passed BOOLEAN, detail TEXT)
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
    v_pass      BOOLEAN;
    v_detail    TEXT;
    v_admin_id  BIGINT;
    v_coord_id  BIGINT;
    v_vol_id    BIGINT;
    v_event_id  BIGINT;
    v_event2_id BIGINT;
    v_post_id   BIGINT;
    v_post2_id  BIGINT;
    v_qr_id     BIGINT;
    v_app_id    BIGINT;
    v_app2_id   BIGINT;
BEGIN
    -- All tests run inside a single cleanup subtransaction so zero rows
    -- (including automatic audit_logs rows) remain after execution.
    BEGIN
        -- Test 1: Invalid blood type rejected
        BEGIN
            INSERT INTO users (phone_hash, phone_enc, display_name, blood_type)
            VALUES (repeat('1', 64), 'test_enc_1', 'Test User 1', 'O_POS');
            v_pass := FALSE; v_detail := 'Should have raised ck_users_blood_type';
        EXCEPTION WHEN check_violation THEN
            v_pass := TRUE; v_detail := SQLERRM;
        END;
        RETURN QUERY SELECT 'ck_users_blood_type'::TEXT, v_pass, v_detail;

        -- Test 2: Invalid account status rejected
        BEGIN
            INSERT INTO users (phone_hash, phone_enc, display_name, account_status)
            VALUES (repeat('2', 64), 'test_enc_2', 'Test User 2', 'banana');
            v_pass := FALSE; v_detail := 'Should have raised ck_users_account_status';
        EXCEPTION WHEN check_violation THEN
            v_pass := TRUE; v_detail := SQLERRM;
        END;
        RETURN QUERY SELECT 'ck_users_account_status'::TEXT, v_pass, v_detail;

        -- Test 3: Donation consistency enforced
        BEGIN
            INSERT INTO users (phone_hash, phone_enc, display_name,
                               is_willing_to_donate, is_willing_to_donate_blood)
            VALUES (repeat('3', 64), 'test_enc_3', 'Test User 3', FALSE, TRUE);
            v_pass := FALSE; v_detail := 'Should have raised ck_users_donation_consistency';
        EXCEPTION WHEN check_violation THEN
            v_pass := TRUE; v_detail := SQLERRM;
        END;
        RETURN QUERY SELECT 'ck_users_donation_consistency'::TEXT, v_pass, v_detail;

        -- Setup temporary admin, verified coordinator, and volunteer
        INSERT INTO users (phone_hash, phone_enc, display_name, is_admin, verification_status)
        VALUES (repeat('a', 64), 'enc_admin', 'SelfTest Admin', TRUE, 'verified')
        RETURNING id INTO v_admin_id;

        INSERT INTO users (phone_hash, phone_enc, display_name, is_admin, verification_status)
        VALUES (repeat('c', 64), 'enc_coord', 'SelfTest Coordinator', FALSE, 'verified')
        RETURNING id INTO v_coord_id;

        INSERT INTO users (phone_hash, phone_enc, display_name, is_admin, verification_status)
        VALUES (repeat('b', 64), 'enc_vol', 'SelfTest Volunteer', FALSE, 'verified')
        RETURNING id INTO v_vol_id;

        -- Coordinator profile starts as pending and is approved by admin
        INSERT INTO coordinator_profiles (user_id) VALUES (v_coord_id);
        UPDATE coordinator_profiles
           SET status = 'approved', approved_by_id = v_admin_id, approved_at = now()
         WHERE user_id = v_coord_id;

        -- Test 4: Availability time order enforced
        BEGIN
            INSERT INTO volunteer_availability_rules (user_id, weekday, start_time, end_time)
            VALUES (v_vol_id, 1, TIME '17:00', TIME '09:00');
            v_pass := FALSE; v_detail := 'Should have raised ck_availability_time_order';
        EXCEPTION WHEN check_violation THEN
            v_pass := TRUE; v_detail := SQLERRM;
        END;
        RETURN QUERY SELECT 'ck_availability_time_order'::TEXT, v_pass, v_detail;

        -- Test 5: Event time order enforced
        BEGIN
            INSERT INTO events (owner_id, current_coordinator_id, title, start_at, end_at)
            VALUES (v_coord_id, v_coord_id, 'Bad Time Event',
                    now() + INTERVAL '2 hours', now() + INTERVAL '1 hour');
            v_pass := FALSE; v_detail := 'Should have raised ck_events_time';
        EXCEPTION WHEN check_violation THEN
            v_pass := TRUE; v_detail := SQLERRM;
        END;
        RETURN QUERY SELECT 'ck_events_time'::TEXT, v_pass, v_detail;

        -- Test 6: Map provider enum enforced
        BEGIN
            INSERT INTO events (owner_id, current_coordinator_id, title, start_at, end_at, map_provider)
            VALUES (v_coord_id, v_coord_id, 'Bad Map Provider Event',
                    now() + INTERVAL '1 hour', now() + INTERVAL '4 hours', 'mapbox');
            v_pass := FALSE; v_detail := 'Should have raised ck_events_map_provider';
        EXCEPTION WHEN check_violation THEN
            v_pass := TRUE; v_detail := SQLERRM;
        END;
        RETURN QUERY SELECT 'ck_events_map_provider'::TEXT, v_pass, v_detail;

        -- Create a valid event and open post
        INSERT INTO events (owner_id, current_coordinator_id, title, start_at, end_at,
                            acceptance_mode, auto_assign_enabled, require_onboarding_ack)
        VALUES (v_coord_id, v_coord_id, 'Valid SelfTest Event',

-- =============================================================================
-- Migration: v0.12.0 Additive Upgrade — OTP Challenge Table & Stored Functions
-- File: postgres_sql/v0_12_0_auth_otp_challenge_upgrade.sql
-- Target Database: PostgreSQL 14+ (Volunteer Coordination System)
-- Purpose:
--   Implements Phase 1 (AUTH-01, AUTH-04) of v0.12.0 Backend-Client Handshake Plan.
--   Adds auth_otp_challenge table bound to auth_otp.id with dual-clock expiry,
--   single-use consumption, deterministic row locking, and cryptographic key separation.
-- =============================================================================

BEGIN;

-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. Table: auth_otp_challenge
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS auth_otp_challenge (
    id                   BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    otp_id               BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES auth_otp (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    challenge_token_hash TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    purpose              TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'login',
    created_at           TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    expires_at           TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    consumed_at          TIMESTAMPTZ,
    request_id           TEXT,
    identity_nonce_hash  TEXT,

    CONSTRAINT ck_auth_otp_challenge_purpose
        CHECK (purpose IN ('login', 'qr_registration')),
    CONSTRAINT ck_auth_otp_challenge_token_hash_len
        CHECK (length(challenge_token_hash) = 64),
    CONSTRAINT ck_auth_otp_challenge_expiry
        CHECK (expires_at > created_at),
    CONSTRAINT ck_auth_otp_challenge_consumed
        CHECK (consumed_at IS NULL OR consumed_at >= created_at)
);

-- Indexes for challenge lookups and expiry scans
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_auth_otp_challenge_otp_id
    ON auth_otp_challenge (otp_id);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_auth_otp_challenge_expires
    ON auth_otp_challenge (expires_at)
    WHERE consumed_at IS NULL;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_auth_otp_challenge_nonce
    ON auth_otp_challenge (identity_nonce_hash)
    WHERE identity_nonce_hash IS NOT NULL;

-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. Trigger Function: Enforce Challenge Expiry <= Parent auth_otp Expiry
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION trg_auth_otp_challenge_before()
RETURNS TRIGGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
    v_otp auth_otp%ROWTYPE;
BEGIN
    SELECT * INTO v_otp FROM auth_otp WHERE id = NEW.otp_id;
    IF NOT FOUND THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'invalid_otp_reference: referenced auth_otp row (%) does not exist', NEW.otp_id;
    END IF;

    -- Invariant: Challenge expiry cannot exceed parent OTP expiry
    IF NEW.expires_at > v_otp.expires_at THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'challenge_expiry_exceeds_otp: challenge expires_at (%) cannot exceed auth_otp expires_at (%)',
            NEW.expires_at, v_otp.expires_at;
    END IF;

    -- Invariant: Challenge purpose must match parent OTP purpose
    IF NEW.purpose <> v_otp.purpose THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'purpose_mismatch: challenge purpose (%) must match auth_otp purpose (%)',
            NEW.purpose, v_otp.purpose;
    END IF;

    RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_01_auth_otp_challenge_guard ON auth_otp_challenge;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_01_auth_otp_challenge_guard
    BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON auth_otp_challenge
    FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION trg_auth_otp_challenge_before();

-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. Stored Function: create_otp_challenge
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION create_otp_challenge(
    p_otp_id               BIGINT,
    p_challenge_token_hash TEXT,
    p_ttl_seconds          INTEGER DEFAULT 180,
    p_purpose              TEXT DEFAULT 'login',
    p_request_id           TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
    p_identity_nonce_hash  TEXT DEFAULT NULL
)
RETURNS BIGINT
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
    v_otp          auth_otp%ROWTYPE;
    v_challenge_id BIGINT;
    v_expires_at   TIMESTAMPTZ;
BEGIN
    SELECT * INTO v_otp FROM auth_otp WHERE id = p_otp_id;
    IF NOT FOUND THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'invalid_otp_reference: referenced auth_otp row (%) does not exist', p_otp_id;
    END IF;

    -- Capped at max 180s challenge TTL and parent OTP expiry: min(issued_at + 180s, otp.expires_at)
    v_expires_at := LEAST(now() + make_interval(secs => LEAST(p_ttl_seconds, 180)), v_otp.expires_at);

    INSERT INTO auth_otp_challenge (
        otp_id,
        challenge_token_hash,
        purpose,
        expires_at,
        request_id,
        identity_nonce_hash
    )
    VALUES (
        p_otp_id,
        p_challenge_token_hash,
        p_purpose,
        v_expires_at,
        p_request_id,
        p_identity_nonce_hash
    )
    RETURNING id INTO v_challenge_id;

    RETURN v_challenge_id;
END;
$$;

-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 4. Stored Function: verify_otp_challenge (Atomic, Deterministic Locking)
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION verify_otp_challenge(
    p_challenge_token_hash TEXT,
    p_code_hash            TEXT,
    p_purpose              TEXT DEFAULT 'login'
)
RETURNS TABLE (
    status     TEXT,
    phone_hash TEXT,
    otp_id     BIGINT
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
    v_chal auth_otp_challenge%ROWTYPE;
    v_otp  auth_otp%ROWTYPE;
BEGIN
    -- Step 1: Deterministic locking order — lock challenge row first
    SELECT * INTO v_chal
      FROM auth_otp_challenge
     WHERE challenge_token_hash = p_challenge_token_hash
       FOR UPDATE;

    IF NOT FOUND THEN
        RETURN QUERY SELECT 'invalid_challenge'::TEXT, NULL::TEXT, NULL::BIGINT;
        RETURN;
    END IF;

    -- Step 2: Purpose validation
    IF v_chal.purpose <> p_purpose THEN
        RETURN QUERY SELECT 'invalid_challenge'::TEXT, NULL::TEXT, NULL::BIGINT;
        RETURN;
    END IF;

    -- Step 3: Lock linked parent auth_otp row
    SELECT * INTO v_otp
      FROM auth_otp
     WHERE id = v_chal.otp_id
       FOR UPDATE;

    IF NOT FOUND THEN
        RETURN QUERY SELECT 'invalid_challenge'::TEXT, NULL::TEXT, NULL::BIGINT;
        RETURN;
    END IF;

    -- Step 4: Check consumption status (single-use constraint)
    IF v_chal.consumed_at IS NOT NULL OR v_otp.consumed_at IS NOT NULL THEN
        RETURN QUERY SELECT 'challenge_consumed'::TEXT, NULL::TEXT, v_chal.otp_id;
        RETURN;
    END IF;

    -- Step 5: Enforce dual expiry clocks
    IF v_chal.expires_at <= now() OR v_otp.expires_at <= now() THEN
        RETURN QUERY SELECT 'challenge_expired'::TEXT, NULL::TEXT, v_chal.otp_id;
        RETURN;
    END IF;

    -- Step 6: Enforce attempt limit
    IF v_otp.attempt_count >= setting_int('otp_max_attempts') THEN
        RETURN QUERY SELECT 'too_many_attempts'::TEXT, NULL::TEXT, v_chal.otp_id;
        RETURN;
    END IF;

    -- Step 7: Compare code hash
    IF v_otp.code_hash = p_code_hash THEN
        UPDATE auth_otp_challenge SET consumed_at = now() WHERE id = v_chal.id;
        UPDATE auth_otp SET consumed_at = now() WHERE id = v_otp.id;
        RETURN QUERY SELECT 'ok'::TEXT, v_otp.phone_hash, v_otp.id;
        RETURN;
    END IF;

    -- Wrong code: increment attempt counter on the exact bound auth_otp row
    UPDATE auth_otp SET attempt_count = attempt_count + 1 WHERE id = v_otp.id;
    RETURN QUERY SELECT 'invalid_code'::TEXT, NULL::TEXT, v_otp.id;
    RETURN;
END;
$$;

-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 5. Stored Functions: Retention & Cleanup
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION purge_expired_otp_challenges(p_retention INTERVAL DEFAULT INTERVAL '1 day')
RETURNS INTEGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
    v_n INTEGER;
BEGIN
    -- Delete consumed or expired challenges older than retention threshold.
    -- Active challenges (unconsumed where expires_at >= now()) are never deleted.
    DELETE FROM auth_otp_challenge
     WHERE (consumed_at IS NOT NULL AND consumed_at < now() - p_retention)
        OR (expires_at < now() - p_retention);
    GET DIAGNOSTICS v_n = ROW_COUNT;
    RETURN v_n;
END;
$$;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION purge_expired_otps()
RETURNS INTEGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
    v_n INTEGER;
BEGIN
    PERFORM purge_expired_otp_challenges(INTERVAL '1 day');
    DELETE FROM auth_otp
     WHERE expires_at < now() - INTERVAL '1 day'
        OR created_at < now() - INTERVAL '1 day';
    GET DIAGNOSTICS v_n = ROW_COUNT;
    RETURN v_n;
END;
$$;

COMMIT;

## Part 1: Global Coding Requirements & Consolidated Specifications

### 1. Architectural Guardrails & Golden Rules
1. **Strict Backend-First Sequencing:**
   - Do NOT touch or refactor mobile UI screens (`OtpLoginScreen.tsx`, `CoordinatorAttendanceScreen.tsx`, `AttendanceRow.tsx`) until Phase 4 (Backend Integration Gate) passes against PostgreSQL and real HTTP.
2. **Three Credentials Separation:**
   - **Client Identity Envelope (CIT):** Application-layer encrypted identity envelope carrying phone over TLS-terminating proxies. Gated behind React Native crypto spike; does not block session challenge handshake.
   - **Auth Session Token (`auth_session_token`):** 256-bit opaque random challenge credential. 180s TTL, single-use, stored server-side only as a keyed HMAC hash. **NEVER** used as an API Bearer token; **NEVER** passed in `Authorization` header.
   - **DRF API Token (`Token <token>`):** Standard DRF auth token returned upon successful OTP verification. Retained unchanged. Passed in `Authorization: Token <token>`.
3. **Exact Database Row Binding & Dual-Clock Invariants:**
   - Every challenge record MUST point to the exact `auth_otp.id`.
   - Invariant constraint: `challenge.expires_at <= otp.expires_at` (max 180 seconds).
   - Deterministic row locking: Lock challenge row first, then linked `auth_otp` row `FOR UPDATE`.
   - Single-use consumption: Replay or concurrent verify attempts on the same challenge fail with `409 challenge_consumed`.
4. **Key Separation & Redaction:**
   - Distinct secrets: `OTP_CODE_HMAC_SECRET`, `AUTH_SESSION_TOKEN_SECRET`, `PHONE_HASH_HMAC_SECRET`, `PHONE_ENCRYPTION_KEY`.
   - Zero sensitive logging: Never log raw phone numbers, OTP codes, challenge tokens, CIT payloads, or DRF tokens.
5. **Truthful Delivery Status & Safe `dev_code` Gating:**
   - Delivery adapter: `ConsoleOtpDeliveryAdapter` remains a narrow local/test adapter.
   - Status reporting: Truthfully report `dev_code_available`, `console_simulated`, or `provider_not_configured`. Never claim SMS was dispatched when no telecom provider was called.
   - `dev_code` isolation: Gated behind an explicit local/test feature flag. Production configuration settings test must prove `dev_code` cannot be exposed even if `DEBUG` is true.
6. **Backward Compatibility & Route Canonicalization:**
   - Retain legacy routes during rollout: `POST /api/v1/auth/otp/request/`, `POST /api/v1/auth/otp/verify/`.
   - Canonical check-in route: `/api/v1/checkin/attendance/manual-checkin/` is canonical for mobile. Root alias `/api/v1/attendance/manual-checkin/` retained on backend for compatibility.
7. **No Fabricated Data & Truth in State:**
   - Never alias `phone` to `email` (P1-01).
   - Never fabricate `checkedInAt = new Date().toISOString()`, never overwrite server method (`qr_scan`/`geo`), and never clear pending geo-confirmation on manual check-in.
   - Never synthesize fake assignments (P1-03) or return hard-coded feedback metrics (P1-04).
   - Keep transport DTOs out of domain repositories and use cases via explicit mappers (P1-05).
8. **Secure Storage Fail-Closed:**
   - In production HTTP mode, never fall back to AsyncStorage or in-memory storage for bearer tokens; `MemoryTokenStore` is strictly for injected tests.
9. **No Speculative POST Retries:**
   - Do not auto-retry non-idempotent POSTs on timeout.
   - Invalidate local session strictly on HTTP 401; never on 403, 404, 409, 429, 5xx, or network timeout.
10. **Deferred Scope Protection:**
    - Dormant backend geo function `geo_check_in()` preserved.
    - No native GPS/map packages, no location permission popups, no mocked coordinates in UI.
    - Friends capability visibly deferred as "Coming Soon".

## Phase 2A — Backend Auth Challenge Service & Safe Dev-Code Guard (Tickets AUTH-02, AUTH-03)

### 1. Scope & Execution Objectives
- Standardize `OTP_CODE_LENGTH = 6` in `backend/services/auth_service.py` with backward compatibility and configurable overrides.
- Implement tokenized challenge service methods:
  - `request_tokenized_login_otp(phone, request_id)`:
    - Normalizes phone and calculates deterministic HMAC hash.
    - Enforces account eligibility and status policies.
    - Generates 6-digit cryptographic OTP and 256-bit opaque challenge token.
    - Atomically persists `auth_otp` and linked `auth_otp_challenge` record in PostgreSQL with strict dual-clock expiry constraints (<= 180 seconds).
    - Supports `request_id` idempotency reissuance to return active challenge without generating duplicate OTPs.
    - Dispatches through `ConsoleOtpDeliveryAdapter` returning truthful delivery metadata (`delivered: False`, `channel: "sms"`, `provider: "console"`, `configured: False`).
    - Gates optional `dev_code` behind `can_expose_dev_code()` which strictly forbids exposing OTP codes in production settings.
  - `verify_tokenized_login_otp(auth_session_token, code, display_name)`:
    - Hashes opaque `auth_session_token` with `AUTH_SESSION_TOKEN_SECRET`.
    - Resolves and verifies challenge exclusively via PostgreSQL stored function `verify_otp_challenge(...)`.
    - Handles database error status codes and translates them to stable domain errors (`invalid_challenge`, `invalid_code`, `challenge_expired`, `challenge_consumed`, `otp_rate_limited`, `account_blocked`, `account_closed`).
    - Atomically consumes challenge and OTP rows, verifies user account status, creates user if absent, and issues authoritative DRF `Token`.
- Update `ConsoleOtpDeliveryAdapter` to report `delivered: False` (never claiming SMS was dispatched).
- Introduce setting `ALLOW_DEV_CODE_IN_AUTH_RESPONSE` in `backend/config/settings/base.py` and enforce `ALLOW_DEV_CODE_IN_AUTH_RESPONSE = False` in `backend/config/settings/production.py`.
- Implement `can_expose_dev_code()` helper checking both `DEBUG` and `ALLOW_DEV_CODE_IN_AUTH_RESPONSE`, strictly suppressing dev codes under production settings module.
- Retain existing legacy `request_login_otp` and `verify_login_otp` service methods unchanged for backward compatibility.
- Ensure sensitive-field redaction keeps phone numbers, raw OTPs, challenge tokens, and DRF tokens out of log records.
- Create comprehensive integration and unit test suite in `backend/apps/accounts/tests/test_tokenized_auth_service.py` asserting all return states, error translations, failed attempt counting, idempotency, and production `dev_code` suppression.

## Phase 2B — Backend Manual Check-In Service & P1 Domain Rules (Tickets ATT-01, MAP-02, INV-01)

### 1. Scope & Execution Objectives
- Update `attendance_service.manual_check_in()` in `backend/services/attendance_service.py`:
  - Return a structured authoritative result dictionary (`ManualCheckInResult`) subclassing `dict` with backward-compatible object attribute access containing `attendance_id`, `event_id`, `user_id`, `status`, `method`, `checkin_at`, `recorded_by_user_id`, and `already_checked_in`.
  - For idempotent repeats on rows already `checked_in` or `completed`, return `already_checked_in=True` while preserving the existing server `method` (`qr_scan`, `geo`, `coordinator_manual`), original `checkin_at`, and any pending geo-confirmation state (`confirmation_status="pending"`), never relabeling to manual or altering server timestamps.
  - Catch and translate a cancelled attendance row transition (rejected by `trg_attendance_guard`) into a stable domain conflict error (`409 invalid_state`) rather than leaking an unhandled DB exception or 500 error.
  - Preserve `get_event_for_manager_or_404(..., require_write=True)` and database trigger authority checks.
- Implement server-side donation master/sub-flag aggregate consistency (P1-02) in `backend/services/profile_service.py`:
  - Partial PATCH updates automatically enforce aggregate consistency across `is_willing_to_donate`, `is_willing_to_donate_blood`, and `is_willing_to_donate_items`.
  - Enabling any sub-flag automatically sets `is_willing_to_donate = True`.
  - Disabling master flag (`is_willing_to_donate = False`) automatically cascades and disables both donation sub-flags.
  - Incompatible payload (`is_willing_to_donate = False` with `is_willing_to_donate_blood = True` or `is_willing_to_donate_items = True`) is rejected with `DomainError(code="invalid_donation_preferences", status_code=400)`.
  - Guarantees PostgreSQL check constraint `CHECK (is_willing_to_donate OR (NOT is_willing_to_donate_blood AND NOT is_willing_to_donate_items))` is never violated.
- Implement transactional volunteer invite response service logic (P1-06) in `backend/services/application_service.py`:
  - `respond_to_invite(user, application_id, accept: bool, note: str = "")`: volunteer operates directly and transactionally on the existing invite application row (`select_for_update()`) rather than creating an extraneous browse application.
  - If `accept=True`: transitions `status` to `accepted`, sets `decided_by_id` to event manager, and satisfies database triggers (triggering auto-assignment if event auto-assign is enabled).
  - If `accept=False`: transitions `status` to `withdrawn`, preserving audit trails.
  - Rejection of already decided applications (`invalid_state`) and unauthorized user response (`ResourceMaskedNotFound`).
- Expand `backend/apps/attendance/tests/test_services_phase7.py`:
  - Implemented `Section5ManualCheckInAcceptanceTests(TransactionTestCase)` covering all 14 Section 5.5 and P1 acceptance cases against real PostgreSQL (active event + onboarding, missing row -> `not_assigned`, inactive event, cancelled assignment -> `invalid_state`/`not_assigned`, missing onboarding, owner-as-monitor -> 403, unrelated coordinator -> 404, idempotent repeat preserving QR/geo method & timestamp, cancelled attendance -> `409 invalid_state`, concurrent duplicate calls race safety, audit note/recorder persistence, donation transition matrix, and invite accept/reject round-trip transaction).

## Phase 3 — DRF BFF Routes, Serializers, `/me/bootstrap/` & OpenAPI Contract (Tickets AUTH-02, ATT-01, API-01)

### 1. Scope & Execution Objectives
- **Auth BFF (`backend/bff/auth/`):**
  - Added `TokenizedOtpRequestSerializer` supporting both `phone` (over TLS) and `identity_token` (CIT envelope), along with `purpose` and optional `request_id`.
  - Added `TokenizedOtpVerifySerializer` which strictly accepts `auth_session_token`, `code`, and optional `display_name`—strictly rejecting/excluding `phone` input from the verification contract.
  - Added response serializers: `TokenizedOtpDeliverySerializer`, `TokenizedOtpRequestResponseSerializer`, `TokenizedAuthUserSerializer`, and `TokenizedOtpVerifyResponseSerializer`.
  - Implemented public (`AllowAny`, empty auth classes) views:
    - `POST /api/v1/auth/tokenized/request-otp/` (`TokenizedOtpRequestView`): creates 180s challenge, returns `auth_session_token`, `expires_in`, `code_length: 6`, truthful delivery metadata (`delivered: false`, `configured: false`), and safe `dev_code` gating.
    - `POST /api/v1/auth/tokenized/verify-otp/` (`TokenizedOtpVerifyView`): verifies with challenge token + code only, maps domain outcomes, issues DRF `Token`, and returns authenticated user identity.
  - Error mapping aligned with Section 4.3:
    - `invalid_identity_token` -> HTTP 400
    - `invalid_challenge` -> HTTP 400
    - `invalid_code` -> HTTP 400
    - `challenge_expired` -> HTTP 400
    - `challenge_consumed` -> HTTP 409
    - `otp_rate_limited` -> HTTP 429
    - `account_blocked` / `account_closed` -> HTTP 403
  - Legacy auth backward compatibility: Retained `/api/v1/auth/otp/request/` and `/api/v1/auth/otp/verify/` with HTTP `Warning: 299 - "Deprecated auth endpoint"` headers and deprecation logging hooks.
  - Registered all routes in `backend/bff/auth/urls.py`.
- **Manual Check-In BFF (`backend/bff/checkin/`):**
  - Added `ManualCheckinResponseSerializer` declaring all authoritative response fields (`attendance_id`, `event_id`, `user_id`, `status`, `method`, `checkin_at`, `recorded_by_user_id`, `already_checked_in`, `id`).
  - Updated `AttendanceManualCheckinView` to use `ManualCheckinResponseSerializer` and return authoritative state; mapped cancelled row DB conflicts to `DomainError(code="invalid_state", status_code=409)`.
  - Documented `POST /api/v1/checkin/attendance/manual-checkin/` as canonical while preserving root compatibility aliases (`/api/v1/attendance/manual-checkin/` and `/api/v1/events/{event_id}/check-in/`).
  - Updated `AttendanceGeoCheckinView` OpenAPI summary and description to explicitly document it as a dormant backend capability not active in the v0.12.0 mobile release.
- **Compact Session Bootstrap Endpoint (`GET /api/v1/me/bootstrap/`):**
  - Added `BootstrapUserSerializer`, `BootstrapCoordinatorSerializer`, `BootstrapCapabilitiesSerializer`, and `UserBootstrapResponseSerializer` in `backend/bff/volunteer/serializers.py`.
  - Implemented authenticated `MeBootstrapView` in `backend/bff/volunteer/views.py`:
    - Returns minimal session identity (`id`, `uuid`, `display_name`, decrypted `phone`, `account_status`, `verification_status`).
    - Guarantees `email: null` (real null, never fallback to phone or fake email).
    - Returns coordinator workspace access status (`status`, `can_access_workspace`).
    - Derives server-side capabilities (`volunteer: bool`, `coordinator: bool`).
    - Highly optimized query count: executes exactly 1 domain query in the view for coordinator profile status.
  - Registered route `path("me/bootstrap/", MeBootstrapView.as_view(), name="me-bootstrap")` in `backend/bff/volunteer/urls.py`.

  - Regenerated OpenAPI 3.0 schema in `backend/schema.yml` via `manage.py spectacular --file backend/schema.yml --validate`.
  - Validated schema syntax, parameters, component definitions, and route documentation without warnings.

## Phase 4 — Backend Integration Gate & Real-HTTP CI Verification (Tickets INT-01, P1-07)

### 1. Scope & Execution Objectives
- **Real-HTTP Integration Test Suite (No Mocks):**
  - Architected and executed real-HTTP integration tests connecting the actual mobile `ApiClient` (`mobile/src/core/api/apiClient.ts`) directly to a live Django server backed by PostgreSQL over real network sockets (`fetch` over TCP), with zero mocked HTTP transport.
  - Built `scripts/seed_integration_fixtures.py` to seed authentic PostgreSQL test records with database-trigger integrity: Event Owner, Current Coordinator, Unrelated Coordinator, active Event, and assigned Volunteers with attendance rows.
  - Implemented `mobile/src/data/__tests__/v0_12_0_realHttpIntegration.test.ts` covering all 6 mandatory Phase 4 real-HTTP scenarios:
    1. **Tokenized Challenge Handshake:** `POST /api/v1/auth/tokenized/request-otp/` -> returns `auth_session_token`, 180s expiry, 6-digit code, truthful delivery metadata (`delivered: false`, `configured: false`) -> `POST /api/v1/auth/tokenized/verify-otp/` (strictly no phone sent) -> issues DRF Token -> `GET /api/v1/me/bootstrap/` succeeds returning minimal identity, `email: null` (actual null, never phone fallback), decrypted phone, and server-derived capabilities.
    2. **Replay & Parallel Verify Safety:** OTP challenge replay deterministically returns `409 challenge_consumed`. Parallel verifications resolve with exactly one 200 and one 409. Bogus tokens return `400 invalid_challenge`. Wrong OTP code returns `400 invalid_code`.
    3. **Production Dev-Code Suppression Smoke Check:** Live Django server with `ENVIRONMENT=production` and `ALLOW_DEV_CODE_IN_AUTH_RESPONSE=False` strictly omits `dev_code` in real HTTP responses over network sockets.
    4. **Authoritative Check-In & Roster Match:** Coordinator loads roster -> `POST /api/v1/checkin/attendance/manual-checkin/` returns authoritative server `checkin_at` and `method` -> refreshed roster matches server state -> repeat check-in returns `already_checked_in: true` with original timestamp and method preserved.
    5. **Authorization & Masking:** Owner-as-monitor blocked with `403 owner_monitor_read_only`, unrelated coordinator masked with `404`, unauthenticated caller denied with `401`.
    6. **Session Invalidation Invariant:** HTTP 401 clears local session token and triggers listeners; non-401 responses (403, 404, 409, 429, 5xx) and timeouts do NOT silently clear local session.
  - Built `scripts/run_real_http_suite.py` test orchestrator capturing commit SHA, execution duration, and saving test artifacts to `docs/integration/v0_12_0_real_http_integration_report.md`.
  - Created `.github/workflows/v0_12_0_integration.yml` CI workflow provisioning PostgreSQL 16, applying schema and upgrade scripts, running backend tests, validating OpenAPI, running mobile TypeScript type checks, running mobile Jest tests, executing the real-HTTP integration suite, and uploading artifacts.

## Phase 5 — Mobile Secure Storage & Hardened `ApiClient` Transport (Ticket AUTH-05)

### 1. Scope & Execution Objectives
- **Declared Secure Token Storage (`react-native-keychain`):**
  - Installed and pinned `react-native-keychain` to exact version `8.2.0` across both `mobile/package.json` and `mobile/package-lock.json` (no unpinned carats `^`).
  - Refactored `mobile/src/core/auth/tokenStore.ts`:
    - Declared `KeychainTokenStore` utilizing hardware-backed Keystore / Keychain (`@volunteer_mgmt:auth_token`).
    - Completely eliminated all references and drivers for `@react-native-async-storage/async-storage` and `expo-secure-store`.
    - Enforced fail-closed semantics in production mode: if secure hardware storage is unavailable or fails, it throws a typed `SessionStorageError` (`code: 'SECURE_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE'` or `'SECURE_STORAGE_WRITE_REJECTED'`), strictly prohibiting silent fallback to in-memory or unencrypted storage.
    - Preserved `MemoryTokenStore` strictly as an explicitly injected test implementation for unit test suites and mocks.
    - Exported `getStorageCapabilityStatus(store)` exposing storage capability metadata (`{ tier, isSecure, isAvailable }`) while strictly guaranteeing zero token exposure in diagnostics.
- **Hardened Mobile `ApiClient` Transport:**
  - Preserved `Authorization: Token <token>` header injection and `401`-only session invalidation invariant.
  - Added per-request correlation ID (`X-Request-ID`): auto-generates a unique correlation UUID/timestamp-hash if not supplied by the caller, or preserves caller-provided `X-Request-ID` headers.
  - Added structured request timing telemetry (`onTelemetry(observer)`): emits `requestId`, `method`, `url`, `durationMs`, `ok`, and `status`/`errorCode`.
  - Added recursive data redaction helper `redactSensitiveData()` to protect against credential leaks in logs/telemetry (redacting `Authorization`, `phone`, `otp`, `code`, `token`, `auth_session_token`, `cit`, `password`, `secret`).
  - Hardened lifecycle cleanup: guaranteed timeout timer clearance and caller `AbortSignal` listener detachment on every exit path (success, 204, 4xx, 5xx, timeout, network error, exception) via structured `finally` blocks.
  - Enforced strict idempotency invariants: non-idempotent POST mutations are never automatically retried; caller-supplied `Idempotency-Key` or `X-Idempotency-Key` headers are preserved and forwarded directly to the backend.
- **Mobile Session Manager Integration:**
  - Updated `SessionManager` in `mobile/src/core/auth/sessionManager.ts`:
    - Handles `SessionStorageError` gracefully in `hasValidToken()` by failing closed (`false`).
    - Preserves session token on all non-401 errors (403, 404, 409, 429, 5xx, timeout, network error).
    - Ensures listener exceptions during 401 handling do not halt subsequent listeners.
- **Comprehensive Unit Testing:**
  - Expanded `mobile/__tests__/tokenStoreAndSession.test.ts` (23 tests): tested MemoryTokenStore, KeychainTokenStore with mock driver, fail-closed `SessionStorageError` on missing/unavailable driver or rejected writes, storage capability status without token exposure, pluggable delegation, and SessionManager invariants.
  - Expanded `mobile/__tests__/apiClient.test.ts` (22 tests): tested URL construction, query serialization, Token header injection, 204 No Content, 401 session invalidation, 403 preservation, correlation ID generation/passthrough, structured timing telemetry, sensitive credential redaction, AbortSignal listener detachment, and non-retry of POST requests.
  - Updated `mobile/__tests__/locationAndSessionProviders.test.ts` to explicitly inject `MemoryTokenStore` for test isolation.

"""
scripts/alter_local_db.py
Automated CLI helper to apply the v0.12.0 database alteration script
(auth_otp_challenge table, stored functions, triggers) to the local PostgreSQL database.
"""
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

# Repository root
REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent

# Database configuration defaults matching backend/config/settings/base.py
DB_NAME = os.getenv("DB_NAME", "volunteer_coordination_db")
DB_USER = os.getenv("DB_USER", "postgres")
DB_PASSWORD = os.getenv("DB_PASSWORD", "postgres")
DB_HOST = os.getenv("DB_HOST", "127.0.0.1")
DB_PORT = os.getenv("DB_PORT", "5432")

UPGRADE_SQL_FILE = REPO_ROOT / "postgres_sql" / "v0_12_0_auth_otp_challenge_upgrade.sql"


def run_migration():
    print("=" * 60)
    print("Volunteer Coordination System: v0.12.0 Local DB Alteration")
    print("=" * 60)
    print(f"Connecting to PostgreSQL at {DB_HOST}:{DB_PORT}/{DB_NAME} as user '{DB_USER}'...")

    if not UPGRADE_SQL_FILE.exists():
        print(f"Error: Migration script not found at {UPGRADE_SQL_FILE}")
        sys.exit(1)

    try:
        import psycopg
    except ImportError:
        print("Error: 'psycopg' module not found. Run from the project virtual environment:")
        print("  .\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe scripts/alter_local_db.py")
        sys.exit(1)

    try:
        conn = psycopg.connect(
            dbname=DB_NAME,
            user=DB_USER,
            password=DB_PASSWORD,
            host=DB_HOST,
            port=DB_PORT,
            autocommit=True,
        )
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"\n[FAILED] Could not connect to database '{DB_NAME}': {exc}")
        print("\nPlease check that PostgreSQL is running and credentials are correct.")
        sys.exit(1)

    print("[OK] Connected successfully.")
    print(f"Executing migration script: {UPGRADE_SQL_FILE.name}...")

    sql_content = UPGRADE_SQL_FILE.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    try:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(sql_content)
        print("[OK] Migration script executed successfully.")
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"\n[FAILED] Error executing migration SQL: {exc}")
        conn.close()
        sys.exit(1)

    print("\nVerifying database objects...")
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        # 1. Check table existence
        cur.execute("""
            SELECT count(*)
              FROM information_schema.tables
             WHERE table_schema = 'public'
               AND table_name = 'auth_otp_challenge';
        """)
        tbl_exists = cur.fetchone()[0] == 1
        print(f"  - Table 'auth_otp_challenge': {'FOUND' if tbl_exists else 'MISSING'}")

        # 2. Check stored functions
        cur.execute("""
            SELECT proname
              FROM pg_proc
             WHERE proname IN ('create_otp_challenge', 'verify_otp_challenge', 'purge_expired_otp_challenges')
               AND pronamespace = 'public'::regnamespace;
        """)
        funcs = [row[0] for row in cur.fetchall()]
        print(f"  - Stored functions: {funcs}")

        # 3. Check trigger
        cur.execute("""
            SELECT tgname
              FROM pg_trigger
             WHERE tgrelid = 'public.auth_otp_challenge'::regclass
               AND tgname = 'trg_01_auth_otp_challenge_guard';
        """)
        trg_row = cur.fetchone()
        trg_exists = trg_row is not None
        print(f"  - Trigger 'trg_01_auth_otp_challenge_guard': {'ACTIVE' if trg_exists else 'MISSING'}")

    conn.close()

    if tbl_exists and len(funcs) == 3 and trg_exists:
        print("\n" + "=" * 60)
        print("[SUCCESS] Local database has been successfully updated to v0.12.0!")
        print("=" * 60)
    else:
        print("\n[WARNING] Some objects could not be verified. Please check the logs above.")
        sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    run_migration()

"""
scripts/run_real_http_suite.py
Orchestrates the Phase 4 real-HTTP integration test suite against PostgreSQL + Django.
Captures commit SHA, execution timestamp, and full Jest output.
"""
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

repo_root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def get_commit_sha() -> str:
    try:
        res = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
            cwd=repo_root,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
        )
        return res.stdout.strip()
    except Exception as e:
        return f"unknown ({e})"


def run():
    print("=" * 70)
    print("Phase 4: Running Real-HTTP Integration Test Suite (No Mocks)")
    print("=" * 70)

    commit_sha = get_commit_sha()
    start_time = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    print(f"Commit SHA: {commit_sha}")
    print(f"Start Time: {start_time.isoformat()}")

    # 1. Run integration tests in mobile/
    print("\nExecuting: npm run test:real-http in mobile/")
    cmd = ["npm", "run", "test:real-http"]
    if sys.platform == "win32":
        cmd = ["cmd", "/c", "npm", "run", "test:real-http"]

    result = subprocess.run(
        cmd,
        cwd=repo_root / "mobile",
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )

    duration = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - start_time).total_seconds()
    print(result.stdout)
    if result.stderr:
        print(result.stderr)

    passed = result.returncode == 0
    status_str = "PASSED" if passed else "FAILED"
    print(f"\nResult: {status_str} in {duration:.2f}s (Exit code: {result.returncode})")

    # 2. Write artifact report
    report_dir = repo_root / "docs" / "integration"
    report_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    report_file = report_dir / "v0_12_0_real_http_integration_report.md"

    report_content = f"""# v0.12.0 Phase 4 Real-HTTP Integration Test Report

- **Date / Time:** {start_time.isoformat()}
- **Commit SHA:** `{commit_sha}`
- **Execution Duration:** {duration:.2f}s
- **Status:** **{status_str}** (Exit Code {result.returncode})
- **Transport:** Real network HTTP sockets (`fetch` over TCP), zero mocks.
- **Backend:** Django BFF with live PostgreSQL database (`volunteer_coordination_db`).

## Test Output

```text
{result.stdout.strip()}
{result.stderr.strip()}
```

## Verified Scenarios

1. **Tokenized Challenge Handshake:** `POST /api/v1/auth/tokenized/request-otp/` -> `auth_session_token` -> `POST /api/v1/auth/tokenized/verify-otp/` (no phone) -> DRF `Token` -> `GET /api/v1/me/bootstrap/` succeeds with `email: null` and decrypted `phone`.
2. **Replay & Parallel Verify Safety:** OTP challenge replay deterministically returns `409 challenge_consumed`. Parallel verifications resolve with exactly one 200 and one 409. Bogus tokens return `400 invalid_challenge`.
3. **Production Dev-Code Suppression:** Live Django server with `ENVIRONMENT=production` and `ALLOW_DEV_CODE_IN_AUTH_RESPONSE=False` strictly omits `dev_code` in real HTTP responses.
4. **Authoritative Check-In & Roster Match:** Coordinator loads roster -> `POST /api/v1/checkin/attendance/manual-checkin/` returns authoritative server `checkin_at` and `method` -> refreshed roster matches server state -> repeat check-in is idempotent.
5. **Authorization & Masking:** Owner-as-monitor blocked (`403 owner_monitor_read_only`), unrelated coordinator masked (`404`), unauthenticated caller denied (`401`).
6. **Session Invalidation:** HTTP 401 clears local session token and triggers listeners; non-401 responses (403, 404, 409, 429, 5xx) and timeouts do NOT silently clear local session.
"""

    with open(report_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(report_content)

    print(f"\nSaved integration report to: {report_file}")
    sys.exit(result.returncode)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    run()

"""
scripts/seed_integration_fixtures.py
Seeds test data into PostgreSQL for real-HTTP integration testing (Phase 4).
Outputs JSON metadata containing IDs and Tokens.
"""
import json
import os
import secrets
import sys
from datetime import timedelta
from pathlib import Path

# Ensure backend is on PYTHONPATH
repo_root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(repo_root / "backend"))

os.environ.setdefault("DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE", "config.settings")
import django

django.setup()

from apps.accounts.models import Users
from apps.attendance.models import Attendance
from apps.events.models import EventApplications, EventPosts, Events
from common.utils import compute_phone_hash, encrypt_phone, normalize_phone
from django.utils import timezone
from rest_framework.authtoken.models import Token
from services import coordinator_service, onboarding_service


def _make_user(name, is_admin=False, verified=True):
    raw_phone = f"+959{secrets.randbelow(900000000) + 100000000}"
    ph = normalize_phone(raw_phone)
    user = Users.objects.create(
        phone_hash=compute_phone_hash(ph),
        phone_enc=encrypt_phone(ph),
        display_name=name,
        is_admin=is_admin,
        verification_status="verified" if verified else "none",
        account_status="active",
    )
    token, _ = Token.objects.get_or_create(user=user)
    return user, token.key, ph


def seed():
    admin, _, _ = _make_user("Admin Seed", is_admin=True)

    owner, owner_token, _ = _make_user("Event Owner Seed", verified=True)
    coordinator_service.apply_for_coordinator(owner, "Owner Vetting")
    coordinator_service.approve_coordinator(admin, owner.id, "Approved")

    coord, coord_token, _ = _make_user("Event Coordinator Seed", verified=True)
    coordinator_service.apply_for_coordinator(coord, "Coord Vetting")
    coordinator_service.approve_coordinator(admin, coord.id, "Approved")

    unrelated, unrelated_token, _ = _make_user("Unrelated Coord Seed", verified=True)
    coordinator_service.apply_for_coordinator(unrelated, "Unrelated Vetting")
    coordinator_service.approve_coordinator(admin, unrelated.id, "Approved")

    start = timezone.now() + timedelta(hours=2)
    end = start + timedelta(hours=4)
    event = Events.objects.create(
        owner_id=owner.id,
        current_coordinator_id=coord.id,
        title=f"Integration Event {secrets.randbelow(10000)}",
        start_at=start,
        end_at=end,
        acceptance_mode="auto",
        auto_assign_enabled=True,
        require_onboarding_ack=True,
        onboarding_text="Please wear high-vis vests and safety boots.",
    )
    EventPosts.objects.create(event=event, title="Event Marshal", required_headcount=10)
    Events.objects.filter(id=event.id).update(status="published")
    Events.objects.filter(id=event.id).update(status="active")
    Events.objects.filter(id=event.id).update(start_at=timezone.now() - timedelta(minutes=10))

    vol1, vol1_token, vol1_phone = _make_user("Assigned Vol 1", verified=False)
    EventApplications.objects.create(
        event=event,
        user=vol1,
        source="browse",
        conditions_acknowledged_at=timezone.now(),
    )
    onboarding_service.acknowledge_event_onboarding(vol1, event.id)
    att1 = Attendance.objects.get(event=event, user=vol1)

    vol2, vol2_token, _ = _make_user("Assigned Vol 2", verified=False)
    EventApplications.objects.create(
        event=event,
        user=vol2,
        source="browse",
        conditions_acknowledged_at=timezone.now(),
    )
    onboarding_service.acknowledge_event_onboarding(vol2, event.id)
    att2 = Attendance.objects.get(event=event, user=vol2)

    data = {
        "eventId": event.id,
        "eventTitle": event.title,
        "coordinatorToken": coord_token,
        "coordinatorUserId": coord.id,
        "ownerToken": owner_token,
        "ownerUserId": owner.id,
        "unrelatedToken": unrelated_token,
        "unrelatedUserId": unrelated.id,
        "volunteer1UserId": vol1.id,
        "volunteer1AttendanceId": att1.id,
        "volunteer1Token": vol1_token,
        "volunteer1Phone": vol1_phone,
        "volunteer2UserId": vol2.id,
        "volunteer2AttendanceId": att2.id,
    }

    out_path = repo_root / "mobile" / "src" / "data" / "__tests__" / "integration_fixtures.json"
    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(data, f, indent=2)

    print(json.dumps(data, indent=2))
    return data


if __name__ == "__main__":
    seed()
